papers.title: Direct simulation Monte Carlo for dark matter production and phase-space evolution
papers.abstract: To study the early-universe production of dark matter particles beyond thermal equilibrium often requires solving several coupled Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level. We present a new method to address this challenge using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) based on stochastic interactions of an ensemble of particles. We implement and validate efficient algorithms to describe freeze-out, decays, elastic scattering and number-changing processes within the dark sector. These algorithms do not require a discretisation of momentum space on a pre-defined grid and do not rely on approximations such as thermally averaged cross sections. As illustrative example, we consider a scenario with two-step dark matter production, leading to a bimodal phase-space distribution, and consider the subsequent evolution under elastic and number-changing processes. We show that DSMC is a flexible approach to explore out-of-equilibrium processes and solve Boltzmann equations at the phase-space level in order to predict the abundance of dark matter particles and their effect on structure formation.

papers.title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
papers.abstract: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.

papers.title: Dark Matter Model Implications of a Candidate Sub-halo Near the Sun, and the Data Needed to Discriminate Among Them
papers.abstract: Pulsar-timing accelerations point to a localized mass concentration near the Sun, consistent with a dark matter sub-halo. We work out what such an object implies for the nature of dark matter, organizing the implications by their observable effect: suppression or enhancement of structure formation, internal structure and survival after formation, and emission or scattering by the constituents. We discuss ultralight wave dark matter, thermal and nonthermal warm dark matter, dark acoustic oscillations and dark matter-baryon scattering, elastic and inelastic self-interactions, invisible decays with recoil, primordial black holes, indirect detection, and a possible connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy recoil candidate. We then ask what new data would discriminate among these models. The existing accelerations are measured outside the tidal radius, where they are blind to the interior mass distribution, to the object's velocity, and to the sub-halo population. We identify four routes that lift these degeneracies: accelerations measured inside the halo, which separate point-mass, cuspy, and cored profiles; lensing and accretion, which test whether the mass is compact; the morphology of annihilation or decay emission, which probes the inner profile; and a search for a comoving stellar population, which tests whether the object is dark and measures its velocity. We also contrast this program with pulsar-timing-array searches for transiting dark matter substructure, which probe vastly lighter objects through a different observable.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
papers.abstract: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate that searches of the Fermi-GBM archive and a future MeV gamma-ray mission such as COSI could detect these bursts. We also discuss possible multimessenger counterparts, including fast radio bursts powered by magnetic energy release, kilonovae and $511\,{\rm keV}$ line emission associated with centrifugally ejected neutron-rich matter, and gravitational waves from the rapid collapse and subsequent black-hole ringdown. Together, these signals probe complementary stages of PBH-induced NS consumption.

papers.title: The Cosmic Infrared Background from Population III.1 Supermassive Stars and Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmic infrared background (CIB) that is expected to arise from the Population (Pop) III.1 supermassive black hole (SMBH) formation scenario, which involves early SMBH seeding via supermassive primordial star formation enabled by dark matter annihilation heating. We model the emission from Pop III.1 supermassive stars, including their growth phase, flash ionization phase, and early black hole accretion phase, as well as accompanying emission from lower-mass Pop III.2 stars. The CIB is composed of stellar and SMBH accretion disk continuum radiation, nebular continuum emission, and Ly$α$ radiation redistributed through scattering in the neutral intergalactic medium. Based on the feedback regulated Pop III.1 model of Petkova et al. (2026), our fiducial model assumes $\sim 10^5\,M_\odot$ Pop III.1 stars forming by $z_{\rm flash}=20$ with a comoving number density of $\sim0.2\,{\rm cMpc}^{-3}$. For this model, the combined stellar contribution is less than $1\%$ of existing direct and diffuse CIB measurements. However, the contribution to the CIB from $z\sim6-20$ SMBH accretion is expected to be larger than the Pop III.1 stellar component for average Eddington ratios $λ_{\text{Edd}} \sim 0.01$. Latest CIB observations place constraints of $λ_{\text{Edd}} \lesssim 0.3$ for the fiducial Pop III.1 model during these epochs.

papers.title: Little Red Dots from Primordial Vacuum Bubbles
papers.abstract: Quantum tunneling transverse to the inflaton trajectory can produce $10^6$--$10^8M_\odot$ primordial black holes at the abundance of JWST's little red dots, without the enhanced curvature perturbations excluded by limits on CMB spectral distortions. Rare vacuum bubbles nucleate during a brief interval of inflation and later form black holes, with adjustable mass and abundance and a narrow mass spectrum of percent-level width. The leading constraint, from accretion, is satisfied for a population matching the bright little red dots even if all the emitted radiation escapes as hard X-rays.

papers.title: Refractive Neutrino Mass: Effects of Fluctuations of the Dark Matter Field
papers.abstract: Observed neutrino oscillations can be reproduced by a refractive neutrino mass-squared arising from interactions with ultralight scalar dark matter (ULDM). The wave behaviour of the scalar field gives rise to a fluctuating interference pattern, inducing spatial and temporal variations in the refractive mass that can distort neutrino oscillation probabilities. We simulate the interference patterns of the scalar field in the presence of self-interactions. Using results of these simulations, the oscillation probabilities for JUNO and T2K experiments are computed. We find that the refractive mass scenario remains viable for the complex scalar field without self-coupling for $m_φ\lesssim 10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$. For $m_φ\gtrsim10^{-16}~\mathrm{eV}$, repulsive self-interactions narrow the density distribution, reducing the deviation of the survival probability at the first minimum to $ΔP \approx 0.07$ for an appropriate self-interaction coupling. In contrast, for a real scalar field, rapid oscillations with the Compton frequency distort the probabilities for scalar masses $ 10^{-22}~\mathrm{eV} \lesssim m_φ\lesssim 10^{-10} ~\mathrm{eV}$, and self-interactions do not remove this distortion. This distortion becomes negligible only for $m_φ\gtrsim10^{-9}~\mathrm{eV}$. We explore additional effects which could modify the interference pattern and relax the constraints on the required values of $m_φ$. These include scenarios with multiple scalar fields (the axiverse), the gravitational effects of the Sun and Earth on the granule structure, and interactions with the relic neutrino background.

papers.title: Simulation-based inference for gravitational-wave cosmology: parameter reconstruction of a first-order electroweak phase transition
papers.abstract: The detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) from a cosmological first- order phase transition would be unambiguous evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model, with a strong electroweak phase transition (EWPT) at LISA as a prime example. Reconstructing the underlying model from such a signal is challenging, since the map from the model parameters to the spectrum is degenerate and strong transitions occupy only small and sparse regions of parameter space. We show that simulation-based inference (SBI), a likelihood-free approach applicable to generic SGWB sources, provides a reliable parameter reconstruction despite these difficulties. We first apply SBI to the thermodynamic parameters characterizing the transition, namely its strength, inverse duration, temperature and bubble wall velocity. As a concrete application, we then consider a strong EWPT in a singlet extension of the Standard Model and reconstruct the model parameters from the resulting SGWB. We find that the SBI posteriors agree with those of a likelihood-based Markov chain Monte Carlo analysis, at negligible cost per data set once the network has been trained. Using the network posterior as the proposal for importance sampling with the exact likelihood further corrects its remaining deviations, at a sampling efficiency several orders of magnitude higher than sampling from the prior. SBI thus offers a fast and flexible framework for the cosmological science case of LISA

papers.title: A New Gravitational Wave Power Law from Dissipative Sound Waves in Cosmological Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Power-law behavior in cosmological gravitational wave (GW) spectra reveals the physical nature of their sources. For sound waves generated by cosmological first-order phase transitions, we identify a new high-frequency power law arising from the dissipative evolution of the acoustic source. In a dissipative plasma, the GW spectrum acquires an additional $q^{-2}$ suppression relative to the perfect-fluid result in the late-time, strong-damping limit. The exponent is largely insensitive to the source profile, while the turnover and suppression strength probe plasma transport and the source lifetime. In particular, the turnover frequency in weakly coupled hidden sector plasmas is sensitive to the underlying gauge coupling and can lie in the millihertz band targeted by space-based interferometers, opening a way to probe microscopic plasma dynamics through the detailed GW spectrum.

papers.title: Resonant Cavity Searches for Millicharged Dark Matter
papers.abstract: A plethora of resonant cavity experiments have been designed to search for ultralight dark matter (DM) candidates, such as axion or dark-photon DM. In this work, we show that these same apparatuses can be sensitive to ultralight millicharged dark matter (mDM) with masses $m_φ\sim1-100\,μ\mathrm{eV}$. Similar to axion DM, in the presence of a background magnetic field, mDM acts as an effective current which can excite the modes of a resonant cavity. Importantly, for a cylindrical cavity, axion DM dominantly couples to the transverse magnetic (TM) modes, whereas mDM dominantly couples to the transverse electric (TE) modes. We project the sensitivity to mDM that resonant cavity experiments can achieve if they are able to tune and readout their TE modes. We find that fractional millicharges as small as $ε_m=e_m/e\sim10^{-19}$ can be probed. If mDM constitutes only a subfraction $f_\mDM \lesssim0.2\%$ of the total DM density, competing astrophysical bounds do not apply. In this case, resonant cavities can be the most sensitive probes of mDM in this mass range.

papers.title: Review of Pion and Nucleon Gluon Parton Distribution Functions from Lattice QCD
papers.abstract: Gluons play an essential role in the strong interaction that binds quarks into hadrons, as described by quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Understanding how the fundamental dynamics of QCD give rise to hadron structure remains one of the outstanding challenges in nuclear and particle physics. Parton distribution functions (PDFs) provide a successful framework for describing high-energy scattering processes involving hadrons. However, our knowledge of gluon PDFs remains comparatively limited because of the experimental challenges associated with directly constraining the gluon structure of hadrons. In recent years, a major breakthrough has enabled the calculation of the Bjorken-$x$ dependence of PDFs directly from lattice QCD. Among the available approaches, the large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) and pseudo-PDF frameworks have emerged as the most widely used methods and have produced the majority of lattice determinations of parton distributions. These developments have sparked rapid progress in first-principles studies of the $x$-dependent structure of hadrons, including gluon PDFs of the nucleon and pseudoscalar mesons. In this review, we summarize recent advances in lattice QCD calculations of gluon PDFs {using the LaMET and pseudo-PDF methods}, discuss the current status and impacts of these developments, and highlight the remaining challenges and future opportunities.

papers.title: Self-gravity depletes superradiant clouds
papers.abstract: Superradiant clouds of ultralight scalars around black holes are often modeled as free fields, whose levels grow independently and decay slowly through gravitational-wave emission. We show that this limit is never realized. The cloud's self-gravity redistributes particles between levels, just as in the case of axion self-interactions, and dominates over self-interactions for decay constants $f_a\gtrsim6\times10^{16}\,{\rm GeV}\,(α/0.1)$, with $α$ the gravitational fine-structure constant. Self-gravity depletes the cloud by orders of magnitude and feeds more extended levels, weakening all signals that rely on the existence of a large cloud mass. A binary companion, however, can partly offset the depletion. Any assessment of superradiant signals must therefore account for both self-gravity and the cloud's environment.

papers.title: Modeling the gravitational wave spectrum from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe: constant-in-time and coherent-decay models
papers.abstract: We study the production of gravitational wave (GW) backgrounds from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe, following the Constant-in-Time (CiT) model, presented and validated against simulations of decaying turbulence in arXiv:2201.05630. We extend the CiT model to account for the source decay using a coherent description for the unequal-time correlator (UETC) of the source. We present a generic framework that allows us to study different types of sources. As examples, we discuss the applicability of this framework to the production of GWs from decaying MHD turbulence, sound waves, and bubble collisions in first-order phase transitions. We show that the validity of the CiT and the coherent-decay models presented in this work relies on long decorrelation times of the source. However, as the decorrelation timescale of the UETC becomes short, a resonant term grows on top of the GW spectrum predicted by the CiT model, as found, for example, in earlier analytical studies of GW production from turbulence and sound waves. This model is compatible with previous numerical results and explains why sound waves in a radiation-dominated fluid are more efficient than subrelativistic MHD turbulence in producing GWs, which is no longer the case for relativistic turbulence. The CiT model predicts a generic spectrum that scales as $k^3$ in the IR regime, develops a linear $k$ at intermediate frequencies, and decays as $k^{1-b_Π}$ at frequencies above the inverse correlation length scale of the source, where $b_Π$ is uniquely determined by the type of source and the UV slope of its spectrum. Since the $k^3$ and $k$ scalings always appear for slowly-evolving sources and they are commonly found in studies of GW production, we motivate checking the potential applicability of the CiT to other sources of GWs.

papers.title: Can next generation CMB experiments discriminate between $Λ$CDM and dynamical dark energy? A Bayesian forecast for Simons Observatory and CMB-S4
papers.abstract: The combination of Planck CMB data with BAO measurements from the second data release of DESI has revealed a statistically significant preference for a time evolving dark energy equation of state parameterized in the Chevallier Polarski Linder (CPL) form. When type Ia supernovae are included, the preference reaches a significance of $4.2σ$ with DESY5, $3.8σ$ with Union3 and $2.8σ$ with Pantheon+. These hint at a departure from $Λ$CDM model. Our previous Fisher matrix analysis suggested that future CMB experiments could probe such a scenario without external low redshift data sets. Here we extend that study by performing a full Bayesian MCMC forecast for the Simons Observatory (SO) and CMB-S4 experiments, assuming as fiducial the DESI+CMB best fit in the $w_0 w_a$CDM model. We generate mock power spectra with the Cobaya mock CMB pipeline. To quantify the geometric degeneracy in the CMB between $w_0, w_a$ and the matter density, we compute for each mock the $Λ$CDM "shadow" model that preserves the CMB shift parameter R and produces an equivalent first acoustic peak. SO and CMB-S4 alone cannot distinguish CPL cosmology from its $Λ$CDM shadow since the posteriors in the $w_0, w_a$ plane remain broad and largely overlap. This is more pessimistic than our previous Fisher matrix expectation, showing that the Gaussian approximation underestimates the impact of the geometric degeneracy. Adding BAO and Pantheon$+$ supernovae data, yields $σ(w_0)\simeq 0.05$-$0.06$ for both experiments. However, the resulting preference for dynamical dark energy depends on the BAO data set, for instance, SDSS BAO moves the constraints close to the $Λ$CDM. Our results quantify the discriminating power of future CMB surveys in a Bayesian framework, and highlight the role of low redshift distance probes in establishing or rejecting a dynamical dark energy scenario.

papers.title: Dirac leptogenesis with charged leptons
papers.abstract: Popular frameworks that explain the baryon asymmetry of the Universe (BAU) are electroweak baryogenesis, requiring a first-order phase transition, and Majorana leptogenesis, which relies on lepton number violation in the neutrino sector. Dirac leptogenesis offers an alternative mechanism that avoids both requirements, instead allowing the BAU to follow from previously generated chiral asymmetries that remain out of equilibrium in the early Universe. Conventional realizations of this scenario typically invoke ultra-light Dirac neutrinos. In this work, we generalize the mechanism to include Standard Model charged leptons by assuming that their mass-generating interactions have a UV origin and arise from higher-dimensional operators. For concreteness, the analysis is performed within a Froggatt-Nielsen setup, which allows us to naturally address fermionic mass hierarchies, too, now linked to the BAU, and we show that the proposed mechanism is viable by supercooling the flavon phase transition. The framework predicts a flavon with a (1.7-50) GeV mass, bounded by the non-observation of lepton flavor violation and the requirement for the Universe to not reheat above sphaleron temperatures, which could be indirectly probed by future lepton flavor violation experiments.

papers.title: The origin of the apparent ULX deficit in NGC 3256
papers.abstract: Ultra-luminous X-ray (ULX) sources are bright, off-nuclear X-ray point sources, mostly associated with high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs), with a compact object accreting from a donor star at super-Eddington luminosities. Although their HMXB nature implies a connection to star formation processes, previous works have found that luminous infrared galaxies (LIRGs) appear to have a deficit of ULXs compared to their very high star formation rates (SFRs). Here, we analyze three Chandra observations of NGC 3256, a merging LIRG with SFR ~50-60 Msun/yr. Based on local scaling relations, it could be expected to host between 100-120 individual ULXs, which could have a non-negligible impact on the energetics and feedback processes of the galaxy. We aim to characterize all its detected X-ray point sources to determine if there is a ULX deficit in this galaxy. We also aim to explore the potential impact of host-galaxy obscuration and metallicity in said deficit. We characterize the luminosity of each X-ray point source in each Chandra observation, and use all observations to determine their potential ULX nature and the fraction of transient ULXs, as well as construct a ULX luminosity function for this galaxy. We find that the galaxy hosts 10-15 ULXs, making it one of the most ULX-rich galaxies known to date. While comparison with the ULX/SFR ratio of nearby galaxies predicted as many as ~100 ULXs, we show that, when accounting for its very high metallicity, NGC 3256 does not have a ULX deficit; and may even present an excess. While the high obscuration in LIRGs has previously been invoked to explain the ULX deficit, we conclude that it is not required to explain the ULX to SFR ratio in NGC 3256. If obscuration still plays a role, then LIRGs may actually be significantly more efficient at producing ULXs than normal galaxies (of the same metallicity), in disagreement with previous results.

papers.title: Direct inference of cosmological mass growth via timing of black hole - pulsar binaries
papers.abstract: Cosmologically coupled black holes (CCBHs) respond to the expansion of the Universe, independently of conventional astrophysical processes. Recent CCBH solutions in General Relativity demonstrate evolution of gravitating mass $m_{\rm BH}\propto a^κ$, where $a$ is the cosmological scale factor. This can be tested through the orbital period timing of black hole (BH) pulsar (PSR) binaries. In contrast to previous methods used to constrain $κ$, pulsar timing measurement baselines span decades instead of gigayears, allowing sources of bias to be well-controlled. As a test case, we analyze the globular cluster BH+PSR candidate J0514--4002E (spin $P\sim 5.6~{\rm ms}$, orbital period $P_{\rm b}\sim 7~\rm days$) under the assumption that the companion is a CCBH. Taking the difference between the observed orbital and spin period derivatives removes all kinematic effects, leaving only the pulsar's intrinsic spin-down $\dot{P}_{\rm int}$ as unknown. Setting $\dot{P}_{\rm int} = 0$, its physical minimum, gives a robust upper bound $κ\leqslant 3.95$ at $95\%$ confidence. We estimate $\dot{P}_{\rm int}$ through the population of millisecond pulsars matched in spin and infer $κ= 0.82 \pm 1.67$ and $0.75 \pm 1.54$, using $H_0 = 67.6$ and $73.5\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, respectively. Adopting typical baseline scaling of timing precision, the value $κ= 3$, argued elsewhere to link energized vacuum BH interiors to accelerated cosmological expansion, can be excluded or detected for this $2.35^{+0.20}_{-0.18}\,M_\odot$ companion at $3σ$ and $5σ$ confidence by 2031 and 2036, respectively.

papers.title: Calibrating the cosmic distance ladder for independent dark energy constraints
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological results presented by the DESI collaboration show a clear deviation from the $Λ$CDM model when considering a time-dependent dark energy equation of state. This deviation is strongly driven by the SNe Ia surveys, which all share the same low redshift sample. The ZTF survey provides the current larger SNe Ia sample at low redshift, which will significantly increase the constraining power. In this context, the LEMAITRE collaboration aims to provide new constraints on dark energy parameters using three independent SNe Ia datasets: ZTF, SNLS and HSC. This effort requires robust photometric calibration, with a particular focus on filter transmission measurement and star catalog calibration. The target for LEMAITRE is to control the calibration systematics on distance moduli below 0.4%.

papers.title: Particle physics science communication with grass-roots Instagram: a success story
papers.abstract: Communicating science to the public is an integral part of the work of a research collaboration, not an afterthought. Institutional and collaboration-level social media accounts are often run by professional communicators rather than by practising scientists, and single-scientist ``influencer'' accounts are demanding to sustain. We describe {\em CMSatDESY}, a crowd-sourced Instagram account on which the CMS group at DESY tells its own stories, each member in their own voice. In the first half of 2026, the science communication activities through this reached 140k+ unique accounts and received 250k+ views, with an engagement rate of 7\%. We discuss experiences and best practices that can be used by other groups, and describe how the account doubles as a science communication playground for outreach training for a large particle physics group.

papers.title: Superoutburst Precursors in the Faint SU UMa-type Dwarf Nova KSP-OT-201602a
papers.abstract: We present the discovery and photometric study of an SU UMa-type dwarf nova (DN) KSP-OT-201602a. Korea Microlensing Telescope Network Supernova Program data covered almost four years from 2016 to 2019 in BVI-bands for this field, and discovered this faint SU UMa-type DN. Two superoutbursts (SOs: S1 and S2) and two normal outbursts (NOs: N1 and N2) are observed of which peak brightnesses are V = 18.95 mag (S1), V = 18.69 mag (S2) and V = 19.37 mag (N1), V = 19.11 mag (N2). The phase dispersion minimization analysis on superhump of S1 gives the superhump period of 1.52 hr (= 91.2 minutes = 0.06333 days). The magnitude amplitudes for the SOs are 4.34 mag (S1) and 4.60 mag (S2), and those for the NOs are 3.98 mag (N1) and 4.18 mag (N2). The durations of the SOs are 11.39 days (S1) and 12.00 days (S2), and those for the NOs are 2.68 days (N1) and 3.38 days (N2). Clear evidence of a precursor is identified in S1 before the SO peak and this supports the hypothesis that precursor is an NO triggerring an SO and the superhump, while a potential precursor based on limited data is only observed in S2. While the amplitudes of the SOs appear typical for SU UMa-type DNe, their durations seem to be quite short which might require further model calculations in the future.

papers.title: Square Kilometre Array Science Data Challenge 3b: EoR inference
papers.abstract: We present and analyse the results of Science Data Challenge 3b (SDC3b; https://sdc3.skao.int/challenges/inference), an Epoch of Reionization (EoR) inference exercise organised by the Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) using simulated SKA data. The nine-month challenge, running from October 2024 to May 2025, represents the first community-wide comparison of EoR inference pipelines on common simulated datasets. We consider multiple datasets designed to assess performance on both foreground-free and foreground-contaminated cylindrical power spectra and imaging products, adopting different reionization scenarios and EoR simulation models. We include results from 16 teams, which employ a range of methodologies to infer the posterior distribution of the hydrogen neutral fraction across three redshift intervals spanning z=8.41 to z=6.25. The results show significant inter-team variability of the astrophysical constraints even in the simpler case where only instrumental noise is added to the cosmological signal. This underscores the need for further investigation into the relative contributions of signal modelling, the treatment of instrumental effects, and inference methods to the robustness of the resulting conclusions. Although individual methods can produce biased parameter estimates, the combined average of their estimates remains close to the input values, suggesting that independent approaches can offset method-specific biases.

papers.title: TWIN-2: Timing Solar Radio Bursts between 180-350 MHz Against GOES and Aditya-L1 X-ray Detections
papers.abstract: We have conducted continuous solar observations for approximately two and half years using the Two-Element Interferometer (TWIN) at Gauribidanur Radio Observatory (RRI). During which several solar events have been detected. Our observational period coincides with the maximum events phase of the Solar Cycle 25, providing us opportunity to analyse the evolution of the solar activity. Our analysis of two and half years data show a clear increase in the occurrences of solar events, which is consistent with the expected rise in the solar activity towards the peak phase of the Solar Cycle 25. We further investigate the detected solar radio events using X-ray observations from the space based Aditya-L1 and the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES) satellites. For the automated detection of SRBs, a machine learning suite has been trained. This also serves as an instrument for space weather monitoring. On the 7th of November 2025, a solar storm was detected by our pipeline in realtime. A brief overview of the data-processing pipeline, along with the RFI mitigation techniques employed to identify and characterize the solar events, is also presented. Observation data of two and a half years of TWIN is available for public access. The data has been used in student training programmes on solar radio data analysis, with students carrying out the analysis and contributing to the initial analysis of the detected events.

papers.title: Progress in measurements of the CKM angle $γ$ and charm mixing at LHCb
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
papers.abstract: Measurements of the CKM angle $γ$ and of the charm mixing and $C\!P$-violation parameters enable stringent and complementary tests of the weak sector of the Standard Model. The two categories of measurements are intimately related, since they both depend on hadronic parameters of $D^0$ meson decays, and knowledge of charm mixing is required to determine $γ$. The progress made in these sectors at the LHCb experiment is reviewed, and a new simultaneous combination of all relevant LHCb measurements is presented. The combination includes measurements based on data collected during 2011-2018, as well as the first measurement of $γ$ with data collected in 2024. The results, $γ= (63.2^{+2.3}_{-2.2})^{\circ}$ modulo $180^{\circ}$, $x_{12} = (4.2^{+0.4}_{-0.5})\times10^{-3}$, $y_{12} = (6.18^{+0.17}_{-0.18})\times10^{-3}$, $φ^M_2 = (4^{+11}_{-10})\,\mathrm{mrad}$ and $φ^Γ_2 = (19^{+23}_{-24})\,\mathrm{mrad}$, are the most precise to date. The $CP$ asymmetries in $D^0\to K^+K^-$ and $D^0\toπ^+π^-$ decays are also determined under different theoretical assumptions.

papers.title: Impact of Effective Nucleon Mass and Symmetry Energy on Nuclear Pasta Phases and the Unified Equation of State of Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: We investigate how the effective nucleon mass and symmetry energy affect pasta phase properties and the unified equation of state (EOS) of neutron stars. The nonuniform pasta structure is described within the self-consistent Thomas-Fermi approximation, while nucleonic interactions are treated in the relativistic mean-field framework with several typical parameter sets adopted. Our results indicate that the symmetry energy and its slope are crucial in determining the onset of pasta phases and their geometric configurations. In the high-density region where matter becomes uniform, the effective nucleon mass plays a dominant role. A larger effective nucleon mass tends to soften the EOS, which yields a smaller radius for a canonical $1.4 M_{\odot}$ neutron star and reduces the corresponding tidal deformability.

papers.title: The BSM Rollercoaster, 1980-2000
papers.abstract: This contribution is a personal historical retrospective on beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics from 1978 to the early 2000s, organized around its emotional rollercoaster. I trace two waves of optimism separated by a multiyear contraction of confidence, both ultimately ending in disappointment when decisive experimental confirmation failed to arrive. The story begins in 1978, when the Standard Model emerged as the front-runner. It then moves from the first wave of excitement over naturalness and Technicolor, rumored proton-decay events, and the construction of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, to the contraction of confidence in the late 1980s. A dramatic revival came in 1991, when the LEP and SLC precision data pointed toward supersymmetric unification, but it eventually gave way to renewed disappointment over the absence of superpartners and the sharpening of the LEP paradox. I also describe how the realization that Newtonian gravity had been tested only down to distances of order centimeters opened the door to large extra dimensions. Finally, I discuss how Weinberg's 1987 anthropic argument for the cosmological constant, the 1998 discovery of cosmic acceleration, and the emergence of the string landscape changed the intellectual status of naturalness itself and led to Split Supersymmetry. I have tried to describe not only what was proposed, but why these ideas felt compelling at the time, why confidence rose and fell, and how later evidence changed our sense of what could count as an explanation.

papers.title: Probing the Graviton Mass through the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background Last-Scattering Surface
papers.abstract: A nonzero graviton mass makes gravitational waves of different momenta travel different distances during the same cosmic interval. A relic stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) with a finite momentum bandwidth therefore samples a shell of finite thickness, rather than the thin source shell of massless propagation from a single epoch. We describe this effective last-scattering surface by mapping the momentum and emission-time distribution into a radial visibility window in an FLRW background. The calculation uses the geometric-optics propagation relation and includes both dispersion and finite emission duration, without a small-mass or narrow-band approximation. We then calculate how radial averaging changes the angular power for an early-produced background whose momentum channels trace a common source-fluctuation field. For a scale-invariant source spectrum, moving a thin shell leaves its angular power unchanged, so the reduction in power isolates the effect of its finite thickness. For a logarithmic momentum width of $0.5$, mass-to-momentum ratios $q=0.3,1,3$ give angular-power ratios of approximately $0.974$, $0.771$, and $0.508$ at $\ell=10$. At a representative frequency of $3\,\mathrm{nHz}$, these ratios correspond to masses of approximately $3.6\times10^{-24}$--$1.2\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}$. We establish a framework that maps the graviton mass to the SGWB angular power spectrum through its effect on propagation distances and the radial window, for a specified source distribution and frequency selection. Using this framework for graviton-mass inference requires a source and detector model; the calculation here establishes the angular response rather than an observational sensitivity.

papers.title: Testing the Universality of RAR Model with Constraints on Fermionic Dark Matter for M31
papers.abstract: The Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR) model describes dark matter as a self-gravitating system of massive fermions in thermodynamic equilibrium within general relativity. It suggests a dual morphology in galaxies: a highly degenerate quantum core mimicking a central supermassive black hole, and a classical halo that explains galactic rotation curves. Earlier applications of the model to the Milky Way restricted the fermion mass to $mc^{2}=48\text{--}345~\text{keV}$, and the orbits of the S-stars around Sagittarius~A$^{\ast}$ (Sgr~A$^{\ast}$) favored $mc^{2}=56~\text{keV}$, whereas a recent thermodynamic stability analysis allows only $mc^{2}\approx194\text{--}387~\text{keV}$. In this work, we apply the RAR model to the Andromeda galaxy (M31), which hosts a dark compact object of approximately $1.4\times10^{8}~M_{\odot}$ within $0.19~\text{pc}$, roughly 33 times the mass of Sgr~A$^{\ast}$. We solve the relativistic equilibrium equations for $mc^{2}=6\text{--}60~\text{keV}$. For all these masses, the fermionic core lies within $0.19~\text{pc}$ and provides the central mass without a black hole. With a bulge and disk added, the total rotation curve is statistically acceptable ($χ^{2}/N_{\text{dof}}\approx1.18$) but lies below the disk data at $3\text{--}11~\text{kpc}$, an offset attributed to the baryonic models we adopted. The Navarro--Frenk--White (NFW) and Burkert profiles fitted to the same data give a lower $χ^{2}$ but require an additional black hole. The stability of the M31 core against gravitational collapse limits the fermion mass to $mc^{2}\lesssim60~\text{keV}$. With the earlier Milky Way range, a single fermion can therefore describe both galaxies only for $mc^{2}=48\text{--}60~\text{keV}$, which includes $56~\text{keV}$. With the thermodynamic range, no fermionic core can supply the central mass of M31, so M31 would have to host a black hole.

papers.title: Majorana dark matter from a thick-to-thin brane junction: Modal stability, real-mediator coannihilation, and a dark-radiation imprint
papers.abstract: We show that the localized spectrum of a $D=7$ thick-to-thin brane junction can host a thermal Majorana dark-matter candidate. The anisotropy of the wall widths isolates a light junction fermion, which a four-dimensional Majorana mass splits into two nearby states. The factorized transverse profiles impose a modal selection rule on all cubic couplings, and together with the relaxation of the softly deformed background this makes the lighter state stable without an imposed dark parity. Because the localized mediator is a real scalar, identical Majorana particles annihilate in the $s$ wave, and the relic coupling becomes nearly independent of the Majorana mass. The junction sector is a Standard-Model singlet whose light chiral mode is a source of dark radiation. Current CMB data restrict its decoupling temperature and imply $0.05\lesssim\dNeff\lesssim0.076$ for dark-matter masses between $10\GeV$ and $1.5\TeV$, a range accessible to next-generation CMB surveys.

papers.title: $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings at the Large Hadron Collider
papers.abstract: Constraining the $Z$-boson couplings of the $b$ quark, or even ruling out the possibility of an opposite-sign coupling, is considered very challenging at the LHC. Utilizing signatures of new physics resulting from contact operators accompanying the modification of $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings from Standard Model predictions, we show that the ATLAS measurement of $pp\to Zh$ already ruled out the opposite-sign couplings by more than 9.5 standard deviations. We also argue that $pp\to Zhb$, which receives a contribution from the same contact term, would lead to even better sensitivity. Furthermore, we show that with future data this indirect method can provide the strongest constraints on $Zb\bar{b}$ couplings, and can even probe the anomaly in these couplings left over from the LEP era.

papers.title: Two powers, one scalar field: unified early and late dark energy
papers.abstract: We investigate whether a single canonical scalar field can account for both early and late dark energy. We consider a double-power potential in which a steep positive-power term can generate an early peak in the scalar energy-density fraction, while an inverse-power term supports late-time acceleration. This evolution requires the steep term to dominate initially and become subdominant later. We test the model against cosmic microwave background (CMB) measurements, Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) baryon acoustic oscillations, and Pantheon+ supernova data, with the SH0ES host-distance calibration. Relative to flat $Λ$CDM, the data fit improves by $Δχ^2_{\rm data}=-6.90$, or $Δχ^2_{\rm objective}=-3.76$ when Gaussian parameter-prior penalties are included. The scalar-field model gives $H_0=69.53\pm0.26\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, compared with $68.45\pm0.24\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ in flat $Λ$CDM. This shift brings the inferred expansion rate closer to the SH0ES measurement, but does not resolve the discrepancy significantly.

papers.title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
papers.abstract: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface. In both cases the reactor is observed by a small flux monitor detector near the source, while JUNO measures the antineutrino flux at two baselines, suppressing correlated flux and detector systematics. Using the measured Daya Bay per-isotope spectra and its covariance, we model a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) core for the microreactor and a low-enriched uranium (LEU) core for the surface unit, and discuss various potential sources of systematic uncertainties and their impact on the precision of $\thone$. The underground microreactor could improve on JUNO's reach by a factor of three to four, to $\relsth \simeq 4\%$ over a decade, while the surface reactor would reach the present global-fit precision, $\relsth=2.5\%$, in about three years, provided the emission rate is monitored across reactor relocations to the sub-percent level.

papers.title: First $Ω_{\rm m}-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
papers.abstract: Though fast radio bursts (FRBs) are widely advocated as a dark energy probe, no valid $Ω_m-w$ constraint has been obtained exclusively from FRB data to date. Benefiting from a rapidly growing localized sample and a novel statistical framework for modeling the dispersion measure (DM), we report the first simultaneous inference of the matter density $Ω_m$ and dark energy equation of state parameter $w$ from FRBs alone, without external observational priors on these two parameters. We combine a multi-parameter emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum with a physically motivated electron prescription to construct a cosmology-dependent cosmic-DM distribution. Within this unified analysis framework, the mean and variance of DM respond self-consistently to the same underlying cosmology, directly connecting the FRB likelihood to both cosmic expansion and structure growth. Analyzing 125 localized FRBs at $0.105\leq z\leq2.148$, we obtain $Ω_m = 0.33^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ and $w = -0.80^{+0.28}_{-0.38}$ under the flat $w$CDM model. We find a new positive $Ω_m-w$ degeneracy in the FRB posterior, opposite to the strong anticorrelation derived from Type Ia supernovae, offering a complementary test of dark energy properties and highlighting their potential in future precision cosmological studies.

papers.title: Photon-Mediated Axino-Bino Scattering Process for the LZ High-Energy Recoil Event
papers.abstract: We for the first time investigate the photon-mediated endothermic axino-bino scattering process to explain the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy recoil event. We calculate the signals from non-relativistic halo and boosted dark matter (DM), including natural xenon isotopes, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. For a fixed Standard Halo Model (SHM) distribution, a simplified three-bin Poisson analysis yields a best-fit benchmark with mass $m\simeq506\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and mass splitting $δ\simeq326\,\mathrm{keV}$ at the adopted upper coupling bound $g_γ=10^{-3}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. It predicts approximately one accepted event, with $70\%$ in the middle bin. A boosted benchmark with $m\simeq82.87\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and $δ\simeq0.626\,\mathrm{MeV}$ provides a comparable fit. Broader Gaussian incident energy distributions allow fitted masses down to a few GeV. Thus, both the halo and boosted DM scenarios can fit the LZ signal at different DM mass scales.

papers.title: 3D Binary Evolution of a Merging Binary Black Hole Progenitor
papers.abstract: Mass transfer is a highly dynamical 3D process that spans evolutionary timescales in binary stars. It is key to the production of gravitational waves through formation of binary black holes and other double compact objects. We integrate global 3D hydrodynamics into stellar evolutionary modeling to resolve mass transfer across nuclear timescales. We employ the shellular approximation in the stellar evolution code MESA to map a 3D spatial structure by equipotential shells in the Roche geometry to maintain hydrostatic equilibrium across tidally-distorted surfaces. We employ the method of time-incremented multiscale evolution to alternate between stellar evolution and 3D hydrodynamics to span large timescales with dynamical feedback. We employ this framework to examine a likely merging binary black hole progenitor system of a low-metallicity 30Msol donor star and 9.3Msol black hole from the end of the main sequence to core Carbon depletion. We modeled two complete mass transfer phases in 3D while self-consistently accounting for stellar evolution. These comprised a thermal-timescale early Case B phase and a nuclear-timescale late Case B phase. The prescription of Kolb & Ritter (1990) closely predicted the results of 3D evolution, except at the end of the first phase of mass transfer; our 3D model remained well-contained by the outer Lagrange point, despite 1D predictions of substantial L3 overflow during this stage. We find incorporating 3D hydrodynamics during Case B mass transfer did not significantly impact expected merger times. Our model never overflowed L3 as predicted by 1D prescriptions. L2/L3 outflows formed even while underflowing those equipotentials. Our model suggests these outflows can be neglected for the evolution of similar systems, but were dense enough to potentially impact X-ray observations.

papers.title: New unintegrated gluon density in proton and nuclei tested with small $x$ processes at modern colliders
papers.abstract: We present a new unintegrated, or transverse momentum dependent (TMD) gluon density in proton and nuclei. Parameters of the new function have been obtained from a fit on inclusive soft charged hadron production and structure functions at low scales, and from comparison with data on a number of processes at higher scales results taken at LHC and HERA, such as heavy quarks production, prompt photon photoproduction and Higgs boson production. A modification employing the geometric scaling approach has been made to extend the obtained parton density to the case of light and heavy nuclei. As a test of the nuclear TMD distribution we perform a calculation of the charged hadrons multiplicity spectra in pPb collisions at the LHC energies.

papers.title: Interpretation of the LZ Event via Inelastic ALP-Dark Photon Transition with Photon Exchange
papers.abstract: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported a nuclear recoil event at $248\pm23$~keV with a global significance of about $2.6σ$. We for the first time explain it via the inelastic process with photon mediator. We consider a dark matter (DM) axion-like particle (ALP) $a$ converts into a heavier dark photon $γ'$ via the nuclear electromagnetic current, and study the photon-mediated endothermic transition $aA\rightarrowγ'A$. We derive the kinematics and cross sections for non-relativistic halo and boosted ALPs. A three-bin Poisson fit to the LZ data includes the xenon isotopes, charge form factors, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. Halo DM, which has mass $m\simeq1.2$~TeV, mass splitting $δ\simeq346$~keV, and near the upper coupling bound, reproduces the event with about $61\%$ in the middle bin. Boosted DM with $v_{0}=0.05\,c$ and $Φ_{0}=10^{5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ requires only $m\simeq5.74$~GeV and $δ\simeq6.66$~MeV to give about $62\%$. We find that a broader Gaussian spread in the incident energy has a significant effect on the fitted masses.

papers.title: Star-forming disc galaxies align tangentially with the cosmic tidal field
papers.abstract: The alignments of galaxy shapes, with one another and with the large-scale structure of the Universe, have been a topic of considerable investigation within cosmology and extragalactic astrophysics for the last 60 years. Galaxy alignments are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and help us learn about the processes of galaxy formation. Red early-type galaxies are known to show strong radial alignments around other galaxies; however, blue star-forming galaxies have shown little evidence of alignment. We combine SPHEREx spectrophotometry with DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys to build a full-sky catalogue of 71 million galaxies with precise redshifts. With this catalogue we are able to measure alignment signals by splitting galaxies into colour and morphological samples. We detect tangential alignment of blue disc galaxies at $22.5σ$ and radial alignment of red spheroidal galaxies at $65σ$. By measuring the alignment signal separately around overdensities and underdensities, we show that each of these alignments has the scale and environmental dependence of a linear response to the cosmic tidal field; a response purely quadratic in the Gaussian tidal field, as in classic tidal torque theory is ruled out.

papers.title: Strong Field Tidal Disruptions of Rotating Stars by Spinning Black Holes
papers.abstract: We study tidal disruptions of rotating solar-type stars by a rapidly spinning supermassive black hole with general-relativistic smoothed-particle hydrodynamics. To capture strong-field effects, we place the pericentre at a few gravitational radii of a black hole, and compare with weak-field encounters at a larger pericentre around a lighter black hole. We vary the black hole spin, the orbital inclination and the stellar rotation, using rigidly and differentially rotating stars with spin aligned, anti-aligned or perpendicular to the orbital angular momentum. In the strong field, the black hole spin decides whether a core survives on equatorial and inclined orbits, and stellar rotation reduces the surviving core in every partial disruption. At the larger pericentre, as in Newtonian studies, anti-aligned rotation instead protects the star from disruption. In both cases the tide reverses an anti-aligned spin just before pericentre. The outcome differs because in the strong field the tide keeps acting on the reversed core long after pericentre. Deep encounters leave cores spinning above break-up, which shed mass and angular momentum as they settle. Full disruptions approach the canonical fallback law, whereas the late-time slope of partial disruptions is not universal and is set by the debris energy distribution near the surviving core.

papers.title: Predictions for Inclusive Production Cross Sections of the Higgs Boson at the LHC and HL-LHC
papers.abstract: We present updated recommendations of the LHC Higgs Working Group (LHCHWG) for the inclusive production cross sections of a Standard Model Higgs boson in proton--proton collisions at centre-of-mass energies between $7$ and $14$ TeV, including the Run-3 energy of $13.6$ TeV, and for Higgs-boson masses between $120$ and $130$ GeV. All the major production modes are covered. The central values remain consistent with those of Yellow Report 4 (YR4) [arXiv:1610.07922] within the uncertainties quoted there, while the theoretical uncertainties are reduced for most production modes. The improvements rest on specific calculations rather than on a uniform advance: the complete N$^3$LO result in the heavy-top limit together with exact NNLO top-quark mass effects for gluon fusion; the N$^3$LO structure-function calculation supplemented by non-factorisable corrections for vector-boson fusion; the completion of the NLO QCD corrections to the loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ channel for $VH$; NNLO QCD matched to NNLL soft-gluon resummation and combined with NLO electroweak corrections for $t\bar{t}H$, and updated predictions for $tH$; and the matched four- and five-flavour-scheme prediction, with its explicit resummation-scale uncertainty, for $b\bar{b}H$. Since no PDF4LHC recommendation exists beyond NNLO, the mismatch between an N$^3$LO matrix element and NNLO distributions has to be carried as an uncertainty, estimated process by process: it is well determined for vector-boson fusion, whereas for gluon fusion it is doubled relative to YR4. PDFs are now the leading source of uncertainty for the most precisely predicted modes, while residual perturbative uncertainties dominate for the remainder. These results supersede the inclusive cross sections of YR4 and the ad interim recommendations of Ref. [arXiv:2402.09955], and form part of Report 5 of the LHCHWG.

papers.title: Measurements of the total and differential inclusive electron neutrino charged-current cross sections on argon with SBND
papers.abstract: This work presents measurements of the total and single-differential electron neutrino charged-current cross sections on argon using the Short-Baseline Near Detector (SBND) at Fermilab. We present the highest statistics inclusive $ν_e + \bar ν_e$ (95.2% $ν_e$ and 4.8% $\barν_e$) charged-current cross section measurement on argon to date and the first inclusive $ν_e + \bar ν_e$ cross section measurement using the Booster Neutrino Beam. Direct measurements of this channel are crucial for future studies of both long- and short-baseline neutrino oscillations through electron neutrino appearance, which in turn are vital for answering open questions in neutrino phenomenology and searching for beyond the Standard Model physics at the intensity frontier. The data used for this work were collected with an exposure of $8.81 \times10^{19}$ protons on target, and 729 candidate events are selected with a minimum electron energy of 500 MeV. The single-differential cross sections are extracted in electron energy and angle with respect to the beam axis. The flux-averaged total cross section is measured to be $σ= [3.90 \pm 0.18\,\text{(stat)} \pm 0.41\,\text{(syst)}] \times 10^{-39}$ cm$^2$/nucleon for a predicted average neutrino energy of $\langle E_ν\rangle=1.8$ GeV for selected events. The total and differential cross sections are compared to predictions from common neutrino event generators. The data show a preference for generators that predict a lower overall cross section.

papers.title: Low-Latency Alerts of Massive Black Hole Binaries in LISA
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) for days to months before merger, offering opportunities for advance electromagnetic follow-up. To enable such observations, inference methods must provide rapid, continuously updated, and statistically calibrated posterior estimates, while remaining robust to overlapping sources. We present TRUFFLE (Time-evolving Rapid Updates For Follow-up of LISA Events), a simulation-based inference method for MBHBs in LISA data designed to meet these requirements. Our approach uses two networks, selected according to the time to coalescence relative to the end of the analysis window, $Δt_c$. An early-warning network, operating at $Δt_c \in [4~\mathrm{h}, 2~\mathrm{d}]$, estimates the chirp mass, mass ratio, and coalescence time to support electromagnetic follow-up scheduling. A near-merger network, operating at $Δt_c \in [-1~\mathrm{h}, +4~\mathrm{h}]$, infers nine parameters, including the sky position needed for telescope pointing. Both networks process the most recent six days of data using multiband time- and frequency-domain representations, which are summarized by a transformer to condition a normalizing flow. The networks are trained on the full orbit-driven LISA response and amortized over a 30-day range of observation epochs. The near-merger posterior can be corrected through likelihood-based importance sampling, with neural inference taking seconds and likelihood reweighting approximately five minutes on a single GPU. We obtain unbiased posteriors in the presence of overlapping sources, including plunging extreme-mass-ratio inspirals, resolvable Galactic binaries, and additional MBHBs merging up to two hours before the primary merger.

papers.title: Another relation among the neutrino mass-squared differences?
papers.abstract: Determining the absolute neutrino mass scale remains a compelling challenge in particle physics. Establishing precise mathematical connections among the neutrino masses could significantly facilitate this task and shed additional light on the underlying mass-generation mechanism. We highlight the possible existence of a simple algebraic relation between the mass-squared differences, $$\frac{\sqrt{Δm^2_{31}}+\sqrt{Δm^2_{21}}}{\sqrt{Δm^2_{31}}-\sqrt{Δm^2_{21}}}=\sqrt{2},$$ which agrees remarkably well with the best-fit values of recent global analyses of neutrino oscillation data. We then investigate the implications of adopting this relation and how it decreases the number of independent parameters in the neutrino sector. We demonstrate that there are alternative representations well known in quark and charged-lepton physics. Furthermore, we place a tight constraint on the solar neutrino mass splitting, $Δm^2_{21}=(7.445 \pm 0.062) \times 10^{-5} \text{ eV}^2$, and also obtain $Δm^2_{31}=(2.548 \pm 0.041) \times 10^{-3} \text{ eV}^2$. Next-generation reactor and accelerator neutrino experiments are expected to significantly reduce systematic uncertainties. In particular, the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) will measure these parameters independently of each other at the sub-percent level, thereby providing a stringent and direct test of our results.

papers.title: Gamma-Ray Pulsar Discovery Using a Lattice-Based Method
papers.abstract: Pulsars are difficult to discover via $γ$-ray pulsations because typically only one photon is observed per ${\sim}10^8$ rotations. We report the first $γ$-ray pulsar discovered with an extension of a recently proposed algorithm, which uses efficient tools for identifying short vectors in high-dimensional lattices instead of exhaustively searching for periodic signals. PSR J1622$-$7204, an isolated pulsar spinning at 261 Hz, was found in 15 years of Fermi-LAT data using about ten CPU hours. In contrast, the previous state-of-the-art (a semicoherent search) failed after ${\sim}600$ CPU years. This new approach may enable the discovery of many new $γ$-ray pulsars, including in binary systems, a previously intractable problem without detailed prior knowledge of the orbital parameters.

papers.title: Constraints and biases: impact of light-cone effects on power spectrum and bispectrum forecasts
papers.abstract: Next-generation galaxy surveys will map large-scale structure over unprecedented volumes, bringing two goals within reach: constraining primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) and detecting relativistic effects on the largest scales. On these scales, relativistic and wide-separation (light-cone) effects share the scale dependence of local-type PNG, so they must be modelled to avoid biased inferences and to recover the true uncertainties. We present joint power spectrum and bispectrum forecasts that include these effects, with a multi-tracer bispectrum covariance including the odd-parity multipoles and leading non-Gaussian terms. Neglecting light-cone effects biases local-type $f_{\rm NL}$ by $\sim2σ$ for a Euclid-like H$α$ survey and $>10σ$ for a MegaMapper-like LBG survey, mostly through lensing; wide-separation and local relativistic effects contribute $<1σ$. With these corrections included, marginalising over the evolution and magnification biases without informative priors increases the uncertainty on local-type $f_{\rm NL}$ by $\sim60\%$ for a Euclid-like power spectrum and by $\sim50\%$ for a joint power spectrum and bispectrum analysis of the even multipoles. However, the odd-parity multipoles of the single-tracer bispectrum and the multi-tracer power spectrum, which are sensitive to leading-order relativistic corrections, break most of this degeneracy. Non-local shapes are less affected; for these, a bright-faint split of the MegaMapper-like survey improves the joint constraints on the equilateral and orthogonal shapes by a factor of $\sim2$. Finally, local relativistic effects should be detectable at SNR $\sim13$, with a bright-faint split of a DESI-like BGS survey, provided the magnification bias is known to a few per cent, but only marginally, SNR $\lesssim2.5$, for the higher-redshift surveys, and not with the single-tracer bispectrum dipole.

papers.title: Orbital dynamics and gravitational wave of Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter
papers.abstract: The dynamical properties of bound particle orbits around a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole immersed in perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) are investigated. An analysis of the horizon topology shows that both event and cosmological horizons emerge within specific parametric regimes. Curvature invariants, including the Ricci scalar, Ricci-squared, and Kretschmann scalar, confirm the existence of a curvature singularity at $r = 0$. By utilizing the pericenter precession data of the S2 star in Sgr A*, the PFDM parameter is constrained to $0 < λ< 7.726412 \times 10^{5}$ M$_{\odot}$. For a source moving along a periodic orbit, the emitted gravitational waveforms exhibit two key features: (i) the orbital period increases with the ``zoom'' number, accompanied by a modest growth in wave amplitude, and (ii) the PFDM parameter nonlinearly modulates the period, leading to a slight amplitude suppression and introducing only a negligible phase shift relative to the vacuum case. These results explicitly characterize the local imprints of PFDM on relativistic orbital dynamics and offer predictions that are testable by future high-precision astrometric and gravitational-wave observations.

papers.title: Splitting the action: A fully nonlinear fluid method for clustering dark energy
papers.abstract: While the background evolution of dark energy is relatively straightforward to model, its perturbations, especially on nonlinear scales, generally require significantly more sophisticated treatment. Existing simulation methods for clustering dark energy --- a large class of interesting theories which are until now not well studied --- usually rely on grid-based solvers and perturbatively derived equations, whose validity in the nonlinear regime remains unknown. In this paper, we introduce a novel fluid method based on splitting the dark energy action into two parts: a kinetic part and a potential part. The resulting fluid equations are fully nonlinear and not reliant on simplifying approximations, making them suitable to describe the small-scale evolution of clustering dark energy theories, such as $k$-essence models with small sound speeds. We demonstrate the numerical implementation of this framework through spherical-collapse simulations of two representative $k$-essence models, evolving dark matter and dark energy simultaneously. The simulations are able to follow the development of dark-energy density perturbations throughout halo collapse, to $\mathcal{O}(\textrm{1}-10)$. By investigating their dependence on the dark-energy sound speed and dark-matter halo mass, we illustrate how dark-energy clustering responds to variations in the competing effects of pressure support and gravitational pull. These results demonstrate the applicability of this new framework to study nonlinear dark-energy clustering across a range of physical conditions, providing the foundation for its future extension to fully three-dimensional cosmological simulations through particle-based algorithms such as smooth particle hydrodynamics (SPH).

papers.abstract: This study presents the first results for the equation of state of 2+1+1-flavor QCD at the physical point, obtained using the complex Langevin equation. We calculate continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities, such as the baryon density, pressure, the speed of sound and the adiabatic compressibility. The simulations are performed in the isospin-symmetric, strangeness- and charm-neutral setting above the crossover temperature and at unprecedentedly large baryon chemical potentials.

papers.title: Breaking the background and linear degeneracies: Using nonlinear clustering to discriminate between dark energy models
papers.abstract: We show that the traditional approach of parameterizing the background and linear-perturbation evolutions, through the equation-of-state parameter $w(a)$ and a time-dependent sound speed squared $\bar{c}^2_s(a)$, does not fully specify the cosmological behavior of dark energy theories. Using a new, fully nonlinear fluid framework, we perform spherical-collapse simulations of two clustering dark energy models with identical $w(a)$ and $\bar{c}^2_s(a)$, finding that their central dark-energy densities differ by up to 50\% for cluster-sized dark matter halos. We identify the departure of the local sound speed from $\bar{c}_s$ as the main driver of these differences. In contrast, all other theory-specific quantities in the fluid equations can be described by their background values to a very good approximation. The results demonstrate that nonlinear structure formation encodes critical additional information about the underlying dark energy theory, opening an avenue for discriminating between models using observables on small scales.

papers.title: SlotFlow-GB: A Neural Framework for Trans-Dimensional Inference of Overlapping Galactic Binaries
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe the millihertz gravitational-wave sky, including millions of long-lived Galactic binaries (GBs), tens of thousands of which are expected to be individually resolvable throughout the mission's lifetime. Extracting these sources requires jointly determining their number and physical parameters from strongly overlapping signals, posing a computationally demanding trans-dimensional inference problem. We introduce SlotFlow-GB, a neural framework that constructs a learned approximation to the trans-dimensional posterior, producing a probability distribution over source multiplicity and parameter densities for individual binaries in a single evaluation, without requiring their number to be specified in advance. We demonstrate this framework using year-long LISA simulations containing up to ten binaries within a 2 $μ$Hz frequency interval, focusing on a high-SNR regime in which source overlap, rather than individual-source detectability, is the primary challenge. The inferred source count differs from the true count by at most one in 94% of cases, while the model identifies individual binaries even when their signals overlap strongly in frequency. A complete evaluation, including parameter sampling, takes just 41 ms per band on one NVIDIA GH200 GPU, or 530 ms on eight laptop CPU threads. We further demonstrate that these distributions can be used to initialize subsequent likelihood-based inference, connecting fast amortized predictions with joint parameter estimation.

papers.title: The gravitational wave candidate S251112cm: near-complete optical coverage with ATLAS, Pan-STARRS and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
papers.abstract: On 2025 November 12, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) network detected S251112cm, a compact binary merger candidate with a false alarm rate of one per four years at a luminosity distance of $93 \pm 27$ Mpc. The probability that the lighter component's mass lies below 1 $M_\odot$ is >99%, while the probability that either component lies at 1-3 $M_\odot$ is only 8%, leaving the nature of the progenitor system unclear. We present Pan-STARRS and ATLAS optical follow-up of the 90% localisation region, and quantify Vera C. Rubin Observatory target-of-opportunity observations. In the North, Pan-STARRS imaged 1084 deg$^2$ (65%) within 7 days to a median depth of 21.9 mag and ATLAS 1545 deg$^2$ (87%) within 14 days to 19.3 mag across both hemispheres; in the South, Rubin covered 849 deg$^2$ (36%) 2-10 days post-merger to median depths of 24.5 ($g$) and 23.5 ($i$) mag. They reported 173, 93 and 67 candidates respectively (269 unique), which we assess against AT 2017gfo-like kilonova and SN 1998bw-like broad-lined Type Ic supernova models using prior activity, host luminosity distance, photometric evolution and absolute magnitude. Eight survive, mainly for lack of distance information. Six of these lie in hosts fainter than any in a volume-limited comparison sample, suggesting they are background sources. AT 2025aimy declines too slowly for the AT 2017gfo-like model, and a VLT host spectrum places AT 2025alqe outside the LVK volume, leaving no convincing counterpart candidates. Pan-STARRS and Rubin together exclude both models in $\sim$80% of the 90% localisation volume: the deepest wide-area constraint on a subsolar-mass merger to date and, to our knowledge, the most complete optical coverage of a significant subsolar-mass candidate.

papers.title: Sourcing vector perturbations in warm inflation through shear viscous effects
papers.abstract: Vector modes are generally believed not to play a significant role in standard cosmological perturbation theory because they decay rapidly. Non-equilibrium dynamics in the radiation bath present during warm inflation can lead to shear viscous effects, requiring a description beyond the perfect-fluid approximation. We adopt the fluctuating hydrodynamic approach to account for stochastic anisotropic stress related to shear viscosity. We show that the vector mode obeys a constrained Langevin equation in an inflationary background. The resulting power spectrum, considered in the weak-viscosity regime, is proportional to the shear viscosity and it also depends on the Hubble slow-roll parameter $ε$, decaying approximately as $a^{-(1-ε)}$. This behaviour is significantly slower than the unsourced, non-viscous power spectrum, which decays as $a^{-4}$. The continuously sourced vector modes, nevertheless, decay on superhorizon scales, and the illustrative benchmark parameter choices adopted in our numerical examples give a negligible late-time vector-to-scalar ratio. Despite the absence of direct large-scale observable vector signatures, the main results establish a source of vector perturbations during warm inflation and provide a framework for studying possible secondary effects along with large-scale white noises in the vector channel.

papers.title: Nucleon Short-Range Correlations and Supersoft Nuclear Symmetry Energy: Compatibility with Massive Neutron Stars and GW170817
papers.abstract: Massive neutron stars (NSs) require a sufficiently stiff core equation of state (EOS), while the relatively small tidal deformability inferred from GW170817 favors softer nuclear matter at intermediate densities. Given the importance of the nuclear symmetry energy in neutron-rich matter, an intriguing question arises: Can the symmetry energy become supersoft at high densities while remaining compatible with these seemingly competing constraints? Within the nonlinear Walecka framework, we demonstrate that nucleon short-range correlations (SRCs), manifested as a high-momentum tail (HMT) in the nucleon momentum distribution, can accommodate such behavior without introducing additional interaction parameters. We derive for the first time analytical expressions for the symmetry energy curvature $K_{\rm{sym}}$ for both free Fermi gas (FFG) and HMT momentum distributions. Using model parameter sets that reproduce empirical nuclear matter properties around saturation density, we find that SRC-HMT yields substantially more negative $K_{\rm{sym}}$ than the FFG case, allowing the symmetry energy to reach a maximum at low supra-saturation densities and subsequently decrease while the total pressure remains sufficient to support massive NSs. The resulting EOSs also predict smaller NS radii and tidal deformabilities consistent with GW170817. These results connect the microscopic nucleon momentum distribution with the density dependence of the symmetry energy and macroscopic NS properties.

papers.title: The Universality of Halo Growth and Merger Rates in Modified Gravity Theories
papers.abstract: In the standard $Λ$CDM framework, the merger rate of dark matter haloes has been found to follow a nearly universal form, with only weak dependence on halo mass and redshift. We examine whether this universality is preserved in modified gravity (MG) models, where the growth of cosmic structure can deviate from that of general relativity (GR). We use the ELEPHANT suite of large $N$-body simulations to study halo merger rates and mass accretion histories in different modified gravity models, including two representative scenarios beyond-GR: the Hu--Sawicki chameleon $f(R)$ model and the normal branch of the Dvali--Gabadadze--Porrati model. For the mass accretion histories, the modified gravitational effect can produce systematic departures from GR, generally corresponding to more rapid halo growth. The deviations are relatively small when the MG effect is weak, while they become more pronounced in models with strong deviation from GR and can exceed $15\%$ in the extreme case. For the halo merger rate, we find that the nearly universal behavior is well preserved across all the gravity models, with only weak dependence on redshift and halo mass, reflecting the unbiased accretion nature of halo growth. However, apparent deviation from this universality can arise if the halo mass is not defined consistently with the modified gravity model.

papers.title: Multimessenger constraints on the origin of long gamma-ray bursts with plateaus: three cases
papers.abstract: The central engines of long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) with X-ray plateaus remain uncertain. They involve a magnetar or black hole (BH), powered by spin energy and/or accretion. We examine how gravitational waves (GWs) discriminate between these scenarios. For collapsars, we consider three models: (A) a prompt phase powered by hyper-accretion onto a BH, followed by a spin-down-powered plateau; (B) a prompt phase powered by BH spin-down; and (C) a magnetar powering both the prompt and plateau phases. Each predicts a distinct GW signature in timing, energy, and frequency, ranging from broadband emission to a coherent descending chirp. We fit the selected X-ray plateaus of Swift GRBs using the model (A). For GRB~080319C, GRB~111209A, and GRB~130925A, we obtain BH masses of $M_{\rm BH}\sim24$--$124\,M_\odot$, with disc masses of $\sim10\%\,M_{\rm BH}$ at the end of the prompt phase. Mass-scaling of numerical simulations of disc emission yields GW strains of $\sim1.5-1.8\times10^{-24}$ at few hHz. This emission should be detectable by Cosmic Explorer and the Einstein Telescope, with an inferred rate from $0.5$ to $1.5$ yr$^{-1}$. However, ultra-long GRBs powered by tidal disruption events are expected to emit GWs at frequencies ranging from millihertz to decihertz, potentially within the sensitivity range of DECIGO and/or Big Bang Observer (BBO). Current or future detectors may detect GWs associated with BH-powered GRB, but magnetar engines, require next-generation detectors. Current and future detectors could map LGRB central-engine activity.

papers.title: A Surrogate Detector Model for the MINERvA Open Dataset
papers.abstract: The growing availability of open neutrino data promises broader scrutiny of interaction models, but a critical barrier remains: mapping theoretical predictions into reconstructed observables, which previously required computationally intensive methods inaccessible outside the original experimental collaborations. In this work, we present a probabilistic surrogate of the MINERvA detector response, trained on an open simulation dataset to map generator-level final-state particles and interaction geometry to reconstructed observables, without relying on generator-specific interaction labels. We assess its fidelity through conditional response distributions, reconstructed observables, and classifier-based closure tests. We further demonstrate generalization beyond the limitations of conventional phase-space-dependent reweighting by withholding two-particle-two-hole interactions entirely from training and showing that the surrogate reproduces their reconstructed response within the estimated uncertainties. In an end-to-end application to MINERvA charged-current inclusive muon-neutrino data, we reproduce selection efficiencies and purities and forward-fold predictions from GENIE, NuWro, and GiBUU for direct comparison with measurements. By moving theoretical predictions into reconstructed space rather than unfolding the data, this work establishes a reusable interface between neutrino interaction models and experimental observations, expanding the scope of physics accessible through open datasets.

papers.title: Quantum Autoencoder on Real Hardware for New Physics Searches at Muon Colliders
papers.abstract: We apply a quantum autoencoder to search for new physics (NP) in the tri-photon process $μ^+μ^-\toγγγ$ at muon colliders. Using a six-qubit circuit on the Tianyan176 quantum computer, we measure the reconstruction losses for Standard Model (SM) events and anomalous quartic gauge couplings (aQGCs) events. The results demonstrate that the hardware-implemented quantum autoencoder effectively discriminates NP signals from the SM background. Concurrently, we derive the expected constraints on the aQGCs coefficients and compare them with those obtained from conventional methods.
