background.abstract: It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as Hölder continuity. In~\cite{GS01}, M. Goldstein and W. Schlag provided a criterion, based on two simple conditions, for a modulus of continuity to be preserved under the Hilbert transform. These conditions are not satisfied by the weak-Hölder and the log-Hölder moduli of continuity. More recently, A. Avila, Y. Last, M. Shamis and Q. Zhou proved in~\cite{ALSZ21} that for compactly supported $t$-log-Hölder continuous functions ($t>1$) their Hilbert transforms are at least $(t-1)$-log-Hölder continuous. A similar result holds for weak-Hölder continuous functions. In this note we extend these results to a class of continuous functions satisfying a couple of mild integrability conditions.

background.title: Interacting framework for the free magnetic dynamics
background.abstract: This is the second paper of a program aimed at a rigorous many--body theory of continuum fermions in a uniform magnetic field, built on the asymptotic quasi--local structure that the magnetic coherent--state frame induces on the CAR algebra. Here we study the free dynamics. We show that a Bogoliubov dynamics preserves the local structure exactly if and only if it is generated by a function of the Landau Hamiltonian. For this class we compute the hopping coefficients in closed form, prove that the Lieb--Robinson velocity vanishes, and determine when the almost--local algebra lies in the domain of the generator. For the Landau Hamiltonian the dynamics turns out to be periodic. We then describe the ground states and the KMS states at every temperature, prove their ergodicity under magnetic translations, and recover the KMS states at positive temperature as thermodynamic limits of local Gibbs states. Finally, we relate the exact hopping operator to the Hofstadter model. These results confirm that the frame--induced local structure is a consistent setting for the perturbed and interacting magnetic dynamics to be studied next.

background.title: Radiative-recoil corrections at order $α^2 (Z α)^5$ to energy levels of muonium and positronium
background.abstract: We have calculated radiative-recoil corrections at order $α^2 (Z α)^5$ to the energy levels of spin-1/2--spin-1/2 Coulombic bound systems. The corrections we consider involve two exchange photons with two-loop radiative corrections on the electron line. We obtain precise results for all values of the mass ratio. Our results are relevant for upcoming improved measurements of the muonium ground-state hyperfine splitting and 1S-2S interval.

background.title: Degenerate wormhole as a topological oscillator
background.abstract: A spherically symmetric, matter free degenerate wormhole is considered as a gravitational system with a single collective degree of freedom, the radius of its throat. The classical dynamics is determined by applying the equivalence principle to the motion of the throat, while canonical quantization reduces the dynamics to a spectral problem with the dynamical symmetry group \(SU(1,1)\). The exact solution of this spectral problem reveals two qualitatively different regimes. For subPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits Bohr type states characterized by a gravitational Bohr radius \(\hbar^2/(GM^3)\). For superPlanckian masses, the quantum system exhibits a semiclassical regime represented by the Einstein Rosen wormhole with Schwarzschild gravitational radius \(2GM/c^2\). Thus, the model connects the familiar quantum bound state behavior with the semiclassical geometry of a gravitational horizon.

background.title: The 1d Stochastic Dirac Operator
background.abstract: We introduce a random Dirac operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R}^2)$ that we call $1d$ Stochastic Dirac Operator and which is indexed by two parameters $κ_0,κ$. In two companion articles, we show that this operator arises generically as the small disorder limit of one-dimensional random Schrödinger operators, thus revealing a universal behavior. In the present paper, we provide a detailed construction of this singular operator, and investigate its spectral properties. In particular, we show that its spectrum is either absolutely continuous when $κ= 0$, or pure point when $κ>0$. In the latter case, we show that the shape of the eigenfunctions is given by the exponential of a two sided Brownian motion with drift, in connection with a result of Rifkind and Virág. Finally, we establish a delicate convergence result of the sequence of eigenvalues / eigenfunctions from the finite-volume operator to the infinite-volume one.

background.title: 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Geometries and Dynamical Gravity
background.abstract: We study non-Riemannian metric-affine geometries in 2-dimensions. We explicitly show that if the connection of the space is not metric compatible (i.e. the non-metricity is non-vanishing) then the underlying 2-dimensional manifold is not an Einstein manifold, in contrast to the Riemannian case. Furthermore we prove that in general the curvature in such spaces is specified completely by the Ricci tensor which, however, is not symmetric now. An enlarged symmetry of the scalar curvature under vectorial connection shifts is also found. We then apply our results to the study of 2-dimensional Metric-Affine Gravity Theories and discuss some special cases.

background.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
background.abstract: We establish a framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms, surpassing standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. Our three conjectures are as follows: 1. For fixed field content and derivative order, effective couplings form a finite-dimensional space under stated equivalences. 2. A family of mixed RR, gauge, and scalar interactions exists at all orders, represented by a finite number of effective even forms. 3. The higher-derivative contact-term sector can be constructed from a finite set of basic tensor structures using polynomials in derivative symbols. We introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity considerations.

background.title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
background.abstract: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.

background.title: Nodal Knotted Finite-Energy Spatiotemporally Localized Scalar Wave Solutions
background.abstract: Significant amount of information is available in wave optics about monochromatic paraxial beams characterized by nodal knots, the latter being threads of complete darkness (lines of zero intensity) tied into knots. Also, well -known are finite-energy spatiotemporally localized vector-valued wave solutions characterized by knotted to-pologies. Unfortunately, except for solutions to the Schrödinger-like equation describing anomalous dispersion, no scalar-valued spatiotemporally localized waves with analogous knotted topological structures are known to date. It is the goal in this article to fill in this gap by deriving finite-energy spatiotemporally localized scalar-valued wave solutions characterized specifically by Hopf and trefoil nodal knot topologies. This will extend to spatiotemporally localized pulsed fields the diverse important applications of mono-chromatic light beams, having nontrivial topological structures, in trapping and guiding particles, image processing and optical communications; also, in applications to biology and medicine.

background.title: Asymptotics of Hitchin metrics and modularity of exceptional ALG gravitational instantons
background.abstract: We prove asymptotic estimates for the Hitchin metrics on four-dimensional moduli spaces of parabolic $\mathrm{SL}(n,\C)$-Higgs bundles on the three-punctured sphere with flag types corresponding to the Dynkin types $E_6$, $E_7$ and $E_8$. For fixed weights in the alcove interiors and fixed scalar graded residues, the Hitchin metric converges in $C^\infty$ to the semiflat metric along the end. The decay is polynomial in general and exponential when all graded residues vanish. For every admissible parameter with weights in the closed alcoves, the moduli space with its Hitchin metric is a complete nonflat ALG gravitational instanton of order two. Extending the period calculation of Dimakis--Fredrickson--Yae to the boundary and allowing compactly supported changes of marking, we obtain every point of the normalized period domain. It follows from the ALG Torelli theorem that every ALG gravitational instanton with cone parameter $1/3$, $1/4$ or $1/6$ is isometric, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, to one of these moduli spaces with its Hitchin metric.

background.title: Charm and beauty production in pp collisions with ALICE
background.abstract: Measurements of charm and beauty production in proton--proton (pp) collisions provide crucial tests of perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) and unique access to heavy-quark hadronisation. In this contribution, a selection of recent ALICE results, with emphasis on LHC Run 3 measurements, is presented. The transverse-momentum-differential production cross sections of prompt D mesons at $\sqrt{s}=5.36$ and 13.6 TeV and of fully reconstructed B mesons at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV are discussed together with comparisons to theoretical calculations. The rapidity dependence of charm and beauty production and the $\rm D^{*+}/D^0$ and $\rm Λ_c^+/D^0$ yield ratios provide complementary constraints on heavy-quark production and hadronisation. Measurements of the fractions of ${\rm J}/ψ$ and $ψ({\rm 2S})$ originating from beauty-hadron decays, and of the inclusive $ψ({\rm 2S})$-to-${\rm J}/ψ$ production ratio, further constrain the interplay between perturbative heavy-quark production and non-perturbative bound-state formation.

background.title: Notes on non-equilibrium thermodynamics of Robinson-Trautman spacetimes
background.abstract: Robinson-Trautman spacetimes are determined by a parabolic heat-type evolution equation of fourth order for a scalar field on future null infinity. This equation may be re-written as an energy balance for an asymptotically time-like observer. In turn, it becomes a first law in the context of non-equilibrium thermodynamics if the non-linear memory is interpreted as heat. This leads to a local version of temperature and a manifestly increasing entropy density from the viewpoint of the environment.

background.title: Tracing Magnetic Helicity in Interplanetary Space. A Multi-Spacecraft Analysis of the 2024 March 23 ICME
background.abstract: We study the evolution of the magnetic helicity content of an ICME event by inferring its magnetic-field-related quantities at different stages between the Sun and Earth using remote sensing and in-situ observations. We study an eruptive X1.1 flare/CME event and its associated ICME originating from NOAA active region (AR) 13614 on 2024 March 23 00:58 UT. Using magnetogram data of the AR during the flaring event, along with non-linear force-free (NLFF) magnetic field modeling, we reconstruct the magnetic field in the solar corona and analyze its magnetic helicity budget. The helicity is also tracked in-situ in the heliosphere using four well radially-aligned spacecraft (Solar Orbiter at 0.39 AU, BepiColombo at 0.58 AU, STEREO-A at 0.96 AU and Wind at 0.99 AU) measuring the ICME magnetic field signature. We use different force-free magnetic field models (Lundquist, Gold-Hoyle) to evaluate the helicity values at each spacecraft. With the Gold-Hoyle-based model (expansion-modified force-free model, 3DCORE), we also reconstruct the ICME and its propagation in the heliosphere. We ultimately compare the results obtained for each model and spacecraft to the values computed in the corona to give a general understanding of how the event's magnetic field evolved. The NLFF modeling of the AR indicates a left-handed (negative helicity) flux rope (FR) positioned along a slightly northeast-southwest axis, in agreement with chromospheric and coronal observations (H-alpha, SDO/AIA), and yields a helicity budget computed of $-2.16\pm1.32\times10^{41}~\text{Mx}^2$. The helicity inferred from in-situ modeling methods reveals values in a similar range ($-2.0\pm1.0\times10^{41}~\text{Mx}^2$), but is highly sensitive to the spacecraft crossing position through the ICME. It appears that the results given by 3DCORE are more consistent between all spacecraft, as well as with the values inferred at the AR.

background.title: Pairwise fermionic mode correlations in electric and magnetic backgrounds: Landau-level structure and Schwinger production
background.abstract: We investigate mutual information and logarithmic negativity in fermionic Schwinger pair production in parallel electric and magnetic fields. Using spin-dependent Bogoliubov transformations, we construct the in-vacuum and derive the particle--antiparticle correlations for selected Landau modes. We also consider an initially entangled two-particle state and evaluate the correlations for six bipartitions. The physical Landau-level structure is treated explicitly by distinguishing modes with the same oscillator index from the spin representatives of a common physical Landau level. For matched higher levels, the pairwise redistribution relations retain the electric-only form, with the magnetic-field dependence entering through the Landau-level pair-production probabilities. When the two particle groups occupy different physical levels, the cross particle--antiparticle correlations become unequal, and we derive analytic relations characterizing this asymmetry. We further obtain the local logarithmic negativity from the ordinary partial transpose in a fixed occupation-space basis. Finally, we extend the analysis to a Sauter-type electric field in a constant magnetic background and examine the dependence of the pairwise correlations on the field parameters and Landau-level structure.

background.title: Hard X-ray flux rope anchor points in the October 2024 X9 flare
background.abstract: In recent studies, signatures of non-thermal hard X-ray (HXR) emission at the anchor point of erupting flux ropes were reported, suggesting that accelerated electrons trapped in the erupting flux ropes can reach the chromosphere and produce Bremsstrahlung emission there. We investigated the HXR sources observed during the impulsive phase of the X9-class flare SOL2024-10-03T12:18 from AR 13842 and assessed whether any of the HXR sources are associated with the anchor points of the erupting flux rope. We analysed the evolution and location of the flare ribbon sources and coronal dimmings to diagnose the eruption process by using multi-vantage point data from the Solar Orbiter and Earth-orbiting instruments. We combined this with a pre-eruption non-linear force-free magnetic field extrapolation to reconstruct the initial magnetic connectivity and compare it to the observed flare ribbons and dimming locations. The magnetic field extrapolation shows two flux ropes before the flare onset. Tether-cutting reconnection during the impulsive phase of the flare results in a larger erupting flux rope formed by the reconnection of the two pre-existing flux ropes. The Spectrometer/Telescope for Imaging X-rays on Solar Orbiter observes at least four distinct HXR sources: two flare footpoints and two additional outer sources at the anchor points of the erupting flux rope. These observations corroborate earlier speculations that non-thermal electrons trapped in the erupting flux rope precipitate along the field lines into the denser chromosphere.

background.title: Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications: From Circles to Strings
background.abstract: This review is written with a simple question in mind: what does one need to know to enter the literature on Scherk-Schwarz compactifications? It is organized as a sequence of questions that a graduate student might naturally ask, together with the concepts, calculations, and formal tools needed to work through the literature. The discussion starts at an elementary field-theory level and gradually develops toward more advanced aspects of supergravity, orbifolds, quantum effects, and string theory. Phenomenological applications are deliberately left aside.

background.title: Dynamical Temperley-Lieb algebras from Quiver CFTs
background.abstract: The one-loop dilatation operator of a superconformal planar gauge theory can be written as a sum of local generators. The algebra these generators satisfy is a powerful organising principle for the spectrum. For SU(2)-like bosonic subsectors we show that this algebra can be read off directly from Feynman diagrams, which we identify as a natural graphical language for it. For N=4 super Yang-Mills this simply reproduces the Temperley-Lieb (TL) algebra of the XXX spin chain. After orbifolding and marginally deforming to N=2 superconformal quiver theories, the same recipe yields dynamical generalisations of the TL algebra. In these theories, the faces of the diagrams are coloured according to the quiver nodes, and separated by domain walls corresponding to bifundamental fields. There are two inequivalent SU(2)-like subsectors, which lead to two different TL algebras. One sector is built from the two bifundamental scalars and (in the simplest case) gives a dynamical TL algebra with a colour-dependent loop fugacity in its quadratic relation. The other sector is built from one bifundamental and one adjoint scalar, and (always) gives a novel algebra, in which the cubic TL relation becomes dynamical. In this latter case, we show that each generator of this new algebra is related to a standard XXZ TL generator by a colour-dependent twist. This twist is local and not an algebra homomorphism, and can be written as a dynamical Drinfeld twist. In both sectors, the TL structure provides a natural graphical approach to the spectral problem, as well as clarifying the structure of the irreducible representations of these chains. Finally, we give a preliminary description of the loop models associated to these algebras.

background.title: Topological (in)equivalence encoded in zeros of wavefunction overlaps
background.abstract: Topological equivalence between two gapped band structures is determined by whether their occupied states can be continuously deformed into one another without closing the energy gap or breaking the protecting symmetries. We show that this relative topology can be read directly from the overlap matrix between the two occupied subspaces, in a way that treats Chern and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants within a single framework. The determinant of the overlap matrix defines a global section of a line bundle over the Brillouin zone, which vanishes at the momenta where the map between the subspaces fails to be invertible. A singular connection, whose curvature is concentrated at these zeros, assigns each zero an integer charge given by its phase winding. In two-dimensional class A, the total charge equals the difference between the Chern numbers of the two systems. In class AII, time reversal pairs zeros of opposite charge, and the relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant is the parity of the total charge in half the Brillouin zone; the Kane-Mele Pfaffian is recovered as a special case. The zeros coincide with the gap closings of an interpolation between the two systems, and crystalline symmetries constrain their positions and charges. We illustrate the construction in the Haldane, Kane-Mele, and Qi-Wu-Zhang models, including cases where rotation symmetry alone enforces the zeros.

background.title: Near Infrared HST Images Resolve the Filamentary Emission Knots in Pa 30, the Remnant of the Galactic Supernova of 1181 AD
background.abstract: We report the results of a near-infrared HST WFC3/IR imaging program investigating the sub-arcsecond structure of optical filaments in the Galactic nebula, Pa 30, believed to be a SNIax remnant of the historic supernova of 1181 AD. Using a near infrared filter sensitive to [S II] and [S III] emission lines, a 1.2 micron filter to reject stars, and a deep Gemini GMOS [S II] image to help define the remnant's filaments, we identify 226 knots along radially aligned filaments in 15 fields. Knot median PSF-corrected FWHM is 0.154'' (350 AU at 2.3 kpc) with 32 (14%) unresolved at a PSF of 0.225''. We find that Pa 30's knots are not round but elongated along the filaments. Fitting stacks of knots with their axes aligned to their filament directions and calibrating with artificial knots gives intrinsic sizes of 0.18'' along and 0.11'' across filaments, with about 75% of knots longer when measured along the filament. The minimum nearest-neighbor spacing of knots along a filament is typically 0.6'' (1400 AU) so several times their own size, but can be one-arcsecond or larger in places. This results in 5'' to 15'' long discontinuous chains of separate clumps rather than a continuous structure. We find excellent agreement with recent ground-based Gemini images of Pa 30 when HST images are blurred to the 0.5'' Gemini PSF and conclude that filamentary knots detected in Gemini data are actually blurred HST resolved knots. Finally, we give estimates on the density and mass of sulfur in these knots, set an upper limit on their [Fe II] 1.257 micron flux, and briefly discuss implications for modeling the formation of the remnant's filaments.

background.title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
background.abstract: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $θ=π$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.

background.title: Invariants of subfactors associated to Petrescu's Hadamard matrices of order 7
background.abstract: Petrescu's sixth-root $7 \times 7$ Hadamard matrix defines an irreducible, hyperfinite subfactor $N \subset M$ with Jones index 7. It is built from the spin model commuting square obtained from the Hadamard matrix by iterating Jones' basic construction. We prove that the standard invariant of this subfactor is minimal, i.e. the higher relative commutants consists of Temperley-Lieb algebras. Thus, the principal graphs of the subfactor are the Coxeter-Dynkin graph A$_\infty$. This solves a long-standing open problem. The main new idea is a congruence for the profile of the Hadamard matrix that restricts the order of rotation on the lowest-weight spaces in Jones planar algebra description of the standard invariant. Together with a uniform trace bound, this gives bounded annular multiplicities on a subsequence, which forces the principal graph to have norm at most two. We also show that the same result holds for most Hadamard matrices in Petrescu's one-parameter family. Specifically, the associated subfactors have Temperley-Lieb standard invariant at every transcendental phase and at every algebraic phase with residue $\pm1$ at a prime above three. In each fixed degree the exceptional set is finite and consists of algebraic numbers. Our methods apply to several other families of Hadamard matrices of order $q >4$ as well, and we show that the associated subfactors have A$_\infty$ principal graphs. These include real Hadamard matrices of order $q\equiv4\pmod8$, Hadamard matrices over $\Q(i)$ of order $q\equiv2\pmod4$ and cube-root matrices of order $q$ with $3\mid q$ and $9\nmid q$. For order six Hadamard matrices, we obtain the same result at every transcendental phase in Diţă's family through Haagerup's matrix and at every algebraically independent pair of phases in Karlsson's two-parameter family.

background.title: Coupling of TQFTs to QFTs and SymTFT interfaces from bordisms
background.abstract: M-theory local models may exhibit torsional cycles and other non-trivial topology which interpolate between quantum field theory sectors localized at singularities and the asymptotic regions of the local model. We show that such structures give rise, in standard decoupling limits, to additional topological sectors which can couple non-trivially to the localized QFT. From a symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) perspective, the physical boundary conditions associated to such local models are modified. We give a construction of SymTFT interfaces from geometric bordisms interpolating between the local singularity and the asymptotic boundary. We apply this construction to the circle compactification of a frozen $D_5$ singularity, identifying a topological interface between the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ SymTFT of the full theory and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ SymTFT of its local $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ gauge sector. We show that the resulting coupling between the gauge theory and an additional topological quantum field theory accounts for the apparent mismatch between electric and magnetic symmetries of the frozen theory.

background.title: How Should Candidates Be Weighted under Open-List Proportional Representation? Harmonic Weights and Dirichlet Order Statistics
background.abstract: Candidates in open-list proportional representation systems are not equally prominent, and measurements that involve aggregation over candidates therefore require some form of weighting. We address the question of how those weights should be chosen. Since weights based on realized preference votes are unavailable in advance and endogenous to the electoral outcome, we seek a priori weights that depend on list position alone, and derive them as expected ordered vote shares under a probabilistic model of the division of the list vote among candidates. The natural starting point -- the uniform distribution on the simplex -- is unrealistic, as it prescribes the same degree of concentration of the vote for every list, and under it the leading candidates become more alike as lists lengthen. The other members of the symmetric Dirichlet family require a concentration parameter, which is unknown and which there is no reason to expect to be constant across countries, parties, and elections. Accordingly, we treat that parameter as random. We prove that under a scale-invariant prior restricted to lists with at least two effective candidates, the expected share of the $k$-th candidate decays as $1/k$, and we show that over the leading positions of a long list, up to one hundred of them, the resulting weights are within 1.4 to 3.4 percent, in total variation, of the harmonic weights $(k H_n)^{-1}$, where $H_n$ is the $n$-th harmonic number. No fixed value of the parameter yields similar weights. Moreover, under the uniform distribution itself, harmonic weights are exactly the normalized expected margins between consecutive candidates.

background.title: Naturalness scale inference in chiral perturbation theory and chiral logarithms
background.abstract: We infer naturalness scales of chiral perturbation theory in the mesonic sector using Bayesian techniques that are extended to explicitly take into account chiral logarithms. To demonstrate our approach, we consider the chiral expansion of the pion decay constant $F_π$ and the threshold and subthreshold parameters of $ππ$ scattering. We find a strong observable dependence of the inferred naturalness scales, and show that they need not coincide with the pion mass at which the order-by-order hierarchy of the chiral expansion breaks down. As an application, we discuss the requirements for lattice-QCD constraints on the two combinations of $O(p^6)$ low-energy constants that in the current matching of Roy-equation analyses to chiral perturbation theory need to be estimated from resonance saturation, but could be extracted from the pion-mass dependence of $ππ$ scattering parameters.

background.title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
background.abstract: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge. We show that, under mild regularity assumptions, the rerooting-invariant families of laws satisfying this Markov property are exactly the Boltzmann decorated metric maps. We also prove a strong Markov property and show that the random submaps inducing a Markovian decomposition are exactly the stopping maps for a suitable filtration. Finally, we obtain analogous results for classical decorated planar maps.

background.title: Periods, isomonodromy, and modularity of ALG/ALG$^*$ gravitational instantons
background.abstract: We prove that every smooth ALG or ALG$^*$ gravitational instanton of type $A_0,A_1,A_2,D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3$ is, up to homothety and hyperkähler rotation, isometric to a rank-two wild Hitchin moduli space on $\PP^1$ with its $L^2$ metric. We compute the compact hyperkähler periods and asymptotic parameters of these moduli spaces and give explicit inverse formulas for every admissible choice of these data. For the three ALG types, global isomonodromic transport realizes the two real parameters left undetermined by the compact periods. We use a Hamiltonian variation formula and uniform comparison with the semiflat metric to apply the Torelli and uniqueness theorems.

background.title: Analytic and Numerical Investigation of a Proposed Non-linear Extension of Quantum Mechanics
background.abstract: In this paper, additional properties of a previously introduced non-linear extension of quantum mechanics are investigated. Analytically, we uncover a limit in which the model reduces to ordinary linear quantum mechanics. We also perform a perturbation analysis about an exact solution studied in earlier work. The equations represent a system that is subject to a periodic driver, and we use Floquet theory to help determine its properties. Numerically, we compare the exact solution to the analytic approximation, and we exhibit several examples of how the non-linear effects influence particle trajectories, with particular emphasis on trajectories near the linear limit.

background.title: Hadron masses and pseudoscalar meson form factors in a Poincaré-invariant constituent quark model
background.abstract: We study a Poincaré-invariant constituent quark model with pair, fine-structure, and finite-range three-quark interactions treated in the diagonalization. A fit of 20 parameters to 36 meson and 27 baryon masses gives an rms deviation of $6.85\,\mathrm{MeV}$, with the common offset fixed by a spectral condition. The same mass-fit wave functions give the elastic form factors of ten pseudoscalar mesons in the light-front impulse approximation with the Melosh rotation. The pion and charged-kaon radii are $0.407$ and $0.411\,\mathrm{fm}$, below the measured values. Unlike experiment, the kaon radius slightly exceeds the pion radius. Replacing the pion radial function by the normalized $S$-wave component of the $ρ$ raises its radius to $0.604\,\mathrm{fm}$, showing that hyperfine compression accounts for most of the deficit in the mean-square charge radius. With the light-quark size fixed by the pion, the $K^+$ and $K^0$ radii require strange-quark sizes that differ by $2.2$ standard deviations.

background.title: Entanglement Geometry Beyond Polygons: Graph-Theoretic Entanglement Inequalities
background.abstract: Entanglement entropies of pure multipartite states can be constrained by organizing subsystem cuts as edges (hyperedges) of graphs (hypergraphs). Starting from the one-party entanglement polygon inequality, we derive these constraints from strong subadditivity and pure-state complementarity, with optimal coefficients and explicit equality conditions. Our central result determines, for a distinguished two-party cut and an arbitrary weighted family of cuts, the optimal polygon coefficient: the smallest total weight of the cuts separating a member of the distinguished pair from a remaining party. A refinement involving three mutual information terms gives the exact minimum of the weighted sum at fixed entropies of the two parties and of their union, attained by at most three independent bipartite pure states. This criterion recovers the cycle and complete-graph inequalities and shows that uniform incidence parity, which we prove sufficient for polygon inequalities on hypergraphs, is not necessary. Averaging strong subadditivity over both sides of a bipartition gives a sharp $k$-marginal inequality with coefficient $2\binom{n-2}{k-1}$, and we determine uniformly optimal coefficients for collective hyperstar inequalities. For paths and overlapping hyperchains, the deficits are exact sums of conditional mutual information terms; genuinely multipartite entangled cluster states saturate the hyperchain inequality while the chain inequality remains strict. We characterize pure chain equality states, bound the trace distance to cycle equality states independently of the number of parties and local dimensions, and obtain bond-dimension bounds for matrix product states and sequential-recovery error estimates.

background.title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
background.abstract: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them. This sequence returns the quiver to its original form while transforming the J- and E-terms. We explain the relation between quiver-invariant triality and the orbifold reduction of quiver-invariant brane tilings.

background.title: Second-order formulation of chiral fermions with a local boundary condition
background.abstract: Chiral fermions in $d$ dimensions arise naturally as boundary modes of a massive fermion in $d+1$ dimensions subject to a local boundary condition. When anomalies are absent, this construction can be used to define an intrinsically $d$-dimensional theory of chiral fermions. However, defining the path integral using the first-order Dirac operator with this boundary condition is technically inconvenient, even in the continuum. We present a formulation in terms of second-order differential operators that is completely equivalent to the original formulation in the continuum. Its natural lattice discretization generates Wilson's term and avoids fermion doubling. Our lattice formulation closely resembles the boundary-fermion construction of Shamir, and provides some insight into the case of a general Wilson parameter.

background.title: Optimal long-time derivative estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics
background.abstract: We study the long-time behaviour of derivatives of the semigroup $P_t=e^{t\mathcal{A}}$ generated by the underdamped Langevin (kinetic Fokker-Planck) operator $\mathcal{A}$ on $L^2(μ)$, where the Gibbs measure $μ$ is not required to be finite. Under a weighted relative bound on the Hessian of the potential, we prove that for every integer $m\ge 0$ the squared $L^2(μ)$ norms of $\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ and of $\nabla_{x,v}\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ are bounded by $C_m t^{-2m}\|h_0\|^2$ and $D_m t^{-(2m+1)}\|h_0\|^2$ respectively for large times, and the free dynamics shows that these exponents are optimal. The proof rests on a resolvent estimate near the imaginary axis, valid for every smooth potential, which follows from the adjoint relation between the generator and the velocity reversal and from the Gaussian Poincaré inequality in the velocity variable.

background.title: On Hölder Equicontinuity of the Integrated Density of States for Random Schrödinger Operators on $\mathbb{Z}^d$
background.abstract: We study a random Schrödinger operator $H_λ= H_0 + λV$ on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ consisting of a translation invariant hopping matrix $H_0$ and a random potential $V$, given by independently distributed single site potentials with absolutely continuous distributions. Assuming a regularity assumption for the hopping matrix $H_0$, we show Hölder continuity of the integrated density of states of $H_λ$ up to exponents $2/3$, independently of the disorder strength $λ$.

background.title: Rigid triaxial roto-vibrator in a finite system
background.abstract: We investigate the emergence of rigid triaxiality in a finite system, within the framework of the interacting boson model of nuclei. Appropriate Hamiltonians for a maximally-triaxial rigid shape are constructed. Closed expressions for wave functions, energies and E2 rates for states of the ground band are derived. Classical and quantum analyses reveal that for a fixed Hamiltonian, the system evolves from a $γ$-soft SO(6) structure for small $N$, to a $γ$-rigid structure for large $N$. Attention is paid to symmetry and spectral properties of both rotational and vibrational states.

background.title: Generic arm separation for planar percolation models
background.abstract: Arm separation is an important technical tool in the study of critical and near-critical planar percolation systems. When combined with RSW estimates, it proves quasi-multiplicativity of arm-event probabilities, links the derivatives of different events and allows the identification of universal arm exponents. We provide a very generic statement of arm separation that applies to arbitrary planar percolation models. Our argument is based on exploring configurations conditioned on the existence of arms in such a way that "exposed" arms are revealed with positive probability. The exploration algorithm is independent of the percolation model and applies to all polychromatic arm events. As an application, we prove a strong arm-separation result for critical planar FK-percolation.

background.title: Symmetry-resolved spectroscopy of truncation-induced perturbations in loop tensor network renormalization of the six-vertex model
background.abstract: Tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension $χ$ introduces truncation errors that are amplified by the renormalization-group (RG) flow. For loop tensor network renormalization (LoopTNR) on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, with Luttinger parameter $K$, we identify these errors operator by operator from symmetry-resolved transfer-matrix spectra and conformal perturbation theory. With $O(2)$ symmetry imposed, the dominant error is the dimerization operator, which is allowed because LoopTNR breaks one-site translation. With less symmetry it is the $U(1)$ current or a charge-two vertex operator. The growth of the dimerization per RG step and a parameter-free ratio of its amplitudes agree with conformal perturbation theory to within a few percent. The parameter $K$ drifts slowly, owing to a weak marginal error and to the running induced by the dimerization. A larger $χ$ lowers the initial amplitude of the error for $0.75\le K\le 1.5$ but changes neither the operator nor its growth rate.

background.title: Transition Zone from ExoEarth to ExoVenus: Critical Insight from Planets on the Edge
background.abstract: Venus and Earth, planets with similar masses and radii, provide astonishingly different environments, raising the question of why these two rocky worlds evolved so differently. Explaining this divergence is a central challenge in comparative planetology and astrobiology. Now, atmospheric studies of exoplanets can explore the possibilities of terrestrial planet evolution, especially in the era of JWST; however, we have not yet realized the critical insights rocky exoplanets in the Transition Zone (TZ) can provide. These TZ planets in the overlap between the Habitable Zone and Venus Zone can test how incident stellar irradiation affects surface water retention and habitability. Observations of exoplanets in the TZ can probe not only the emergence and decline of exoplanet habitability but also test hypotheses about Venus' past, complementing upcoming Venus flagship missions. Here, we analyze NASA's Exoplanet Archive, updated with Gaia DR3 data, and provide a target list of 23 rocky exoplanets in the Earth-to-Venus Transition Zone, along with 2 planets in the Venus Evolution Zone (EV). We examine their demographics and quantify their potential for follow-up observations. This list of rocky TZ and EV planets allows observers to optimize target selection and observing strategy for specific instruments. Characterizing exoplanets in the Transition Zone will be critical to investigating open questions about the emergence and decline of habitability on rocky worlds, the evolution from an exo-Earth to an exo-Venus, and Earth's future.

background.title: Weyl-induced ultrasoft renormalization of the static QCD potential
background.abstract: We derive the leading curvature-dependent ultrasoft anomalous dimension of the static color-singlet potential in potential nonrelativistic QCD. In a Ricci-flat background the electric Weyl tensor introduces a $t^{-2}$ term in the short-time chromoelectric correlator. The resulting dipole self-energy is ultraviolet divergent at order $α_s^2$ in the curvature sector, two orders earlier than the flat-space contribution. For $W=C_{μανβ}r^μu^αr^νu^β$ and $V_s^{(W)}=c_W W/r$, we obtain $ν\,\partial_νc_W=C_F C_Aα_s^2/(3π)$. We calculate the compensating soft infrared pole and the finite one-loop matching coefficient in an optical dimensional subtraction scheme. A direct physical-metric fermion calculation reproduces the finite light-flavor term. We also exhibit the cancellation of the leading regulated infrared overlap and the compensating transformation of soft and ultrasoft constants under an evanescent curvature rescaling. In the perturbative adiabatic regime the anomalous dimension fixes the coefficient of a curvature-dependent $α_s^2\lnα_s$ term in the static energy.

background.title: The Clifford Hierarchy from Clifford Stabilizers in 2D
background.abstract: The Bravyi-König theorem limits the constant-depth logical gates of 2D topological Pauli stabilizer codes to be in the Clifford group. Known qubit codes with Clifford stabilizers exceed it by only one level of the Clifford hierarchy, and this was conjectured to hold generally. We show that this bound can be completely bypassed, and that topological codes with Clifford stabilizers in 2D can realize transversal logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy. We present two explicit constructions of codes based on copies of the quantum doubles of $D_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$, with $k$ logical qubits and a logical $C^{k-1}Z$ gate, which is at level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy. The physical circuits realizing the gates consist only of physical $Z$ or $CZ$ gates. The main new ingredient comes from the logical encoding, which depends crucially on non-Abelian group multiplication.

background.title: Variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups
background.abstract: We develop fixed-step variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups, derive their reduced dynamics, and analyze their long-time behavior by backward error analysis. We derive the continuous Euler-Lagrange equations, energy balance, and Noether conservation laws, and construct time-indexed discrete Lagrangians using retractions, with the midpoint-Cayley scheme treated explicitly. On their regularity domains, the resulting phase-space maps are symplectic. For left-invariant discrete Lagrangians, they reduce to Lie-Poisson maps that preserve coadjoint orbits and, when $G$ is connected, every Casimir function. A variational error analysis establishes second-order accuracy of the midpoint-Cayley method. We also construct an exactly symplectic, projectable extension on $T^*(\mathbb R\times G)$ whose formal modified Hamiltonian is affine in the momentum conjugate to time and admits symmetry reduction. Under uniform analyticity, coefficient bounds, and domain-containment assumptions, optimal truncation yields exponentially accurate interpolation and near-conservation of the modified extended Hamiltonian over exponentially long intervals. For a connected attitude network on $SO(3)^N$ with damping and uniformly positive, non-increasing coupling weights, we prove local asymptotic stability of the static consensus set for the continuous dynamics and exact preservation of total spatial momentum by the discrete scheme. Numerical experiments on the network and on a time-dependent rigid body on $SO(3)$ illustrate second-order convergence and the extended energy balance.

background.title: Multiple blobs following a coronal mass ejection
background.abstract: In this paper, we study a partial filament eruption, which generated a C4.1 class two-ribbon flare and a wide coronal mass ejection (CME) propagating in the northeast direction on 2023 March 20. The long, sigmoidal filament in active region 13258 is composed of two parts: the eruptive part and remaining part. Both of them are supported by magnetic flux ropes. The separation of two ribbons persist for ~12 hr, with the separation speeds decreasing from 0.26-5.62 to 0.13-0.53 km/s observed in H$α$ and 304 Å. A thin, curved current sheet follows the CME and extends in the northeast direction. Eight and seven bright blobs are found to move outward along the current sheet observed by SOHO/LASCO and STEREO-A/COR2, respectively. In LASCO images, the apparent speeds, lifetime, maximal height, and width of the blobs are 378-871 km/s, 7-84 minutes, 2.94-6.25\,$R_{\sun}$, and 38.8-225.4 Mm. In COR2 images, the apparent speeds, lifetime, maximal height, and width of the blobs are 336-712 km/s, 20-100 minutes, 4.09-7.61\,$R_{\sun}$, and 102.9-318.3 Mm. A positive correlation is found between the lifetime and maximal height, suggesting that blobs with longer lifetime propagate further from the solar surface. The total duration of blobs is >8 hr, which is consistent with ongoing flare reconnection manifested by persistent ribbon separation in the chromosphere. The aspect ratio (28-37) of the current sheet is probably larger than the critical value, suggesting that the blobs following the CME are possibly generated by tearing-mode instability of the current sheet.

background.title: AI-Native Industrial Control Systems: An Agent Architecture for the Control System Lifecycle
background.abstract: Industrial control systems increasingly use AI for perception, control, and engineering, while available control functions and execution environments are typically established in advance. This paper proposes an AI-native industrial control system in which collaborating agents determine the capabilities required by a task, construct the control application, and prepare its execution environment. System-level agents coordinate device-level agents within configured resource and permission constraints. A physical sorting workstation illustrates two forms of adaptation. In the first case, controller and robot agents construct a sorting application on a prescribed Raspberry Pi target. In the second, a camera agent adds inspection on an edge node, and the controller associates inspection results with downstream pickup decisions. A subsequent revision enables selective sorting using the same agents and deployment arrangement. The trials demonstrate the feasibility of task-driven construction and evolution on the workstation. Commissioning also reveals limitations in the traceability of design decisions, adherence to delegated responsibilities, diagnostic reasoning, and verification of physical behavior.

background.title: Twist and Shout: defect lines on the Rényi torus
background.abstract: We consider what the entanglement between two regions of a critical system can reveal about its symmetries, including non-invertible ones. For two intervals in a two-dimensional conformal field theory, the second Rényi entropy is a partition function on a torus, and a topological defect line can be wrapped around one of the intervals. For an on-site symmetry this computes the overlap of the reduced density matrix with its image under the symmetry acting on one interval, and in general it defines an observable that depends only on the cross-ratio. As the intervals approach each other, the observable vanishes at a rate set by the lightest operator on which the line can end, and its monodromy is fixed by the spins of such operators. Since these spins are constrained by the fusion category, the observable detects 't Hooft anomalies and distinguishes categories with the same fusion rules. It can be computed in closed form for a $\mathbb{Z}_2$, a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ and a Fibonacci line of the $(E_8)_1$ theory, and for the spin-flip and Kramers-Wannier lines of the Ising model, where the spin-flip result agrees with an exact computation in the critical Ising chain. Averaged over a symmetry, the observable reduces to a known Jones-index bound on the mutual information. We also show that the associated twist-field crossing equations are a form of the modular bootstrap, and discuss whether the full fusion category can be recovered from entanglement on surfaces of higher genus.

background.title: Where Did the Angular Momentum Go? WASP-12 b May Have Circularized on a Retrograde Orbit
background.abstract: WASP-12 b is the only exoplanet with confirmed orbital decay. Angular momentum transferred from its decaying orbit should have realigned the star's thin convective layer, yet an earlier Rossiter--McLaughlin (RM) measurement suggested a $\sim$60$^\circ$ spin--orbit misalignment. We present two new Keck Planet Finder RM measurements. We measure a sky-projected obliquity of $λ=-1.3\pm8.7^\circ$; and the star's projected rotation velocity is $v\sin i_\star=1.3\pm0.1~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, an order of magnitude lower than expected for a star of its mass and age. With WASP-12's low chromospheric activity, $\log R^\prime_{\rm HK}=-5.5$, our analysis favors an aligned system in which $v\sin i_\star$ reflects slow surface rotation with $P_{\rm rot}\sim60$ days, rather than a projection effect. Our evolution models favor a late-main-sequence star rather than a subgiant, with a central convective core found in 99\% of posterior samples. This internal structure suppresses the central-focusing and nonlinear wave-breaking mechanisms for inward-propagating gravity waves. We propose that WASP-12 b was initially placed on a retrograde orbit after high-eccentricity migration, when its host rotated at $v\sin i_\star\approx14$~km~s$^{-1}$ (or $P_{\rm rot}\sim$6 days). Tidal decay transferred orbital angular momentum to the convective envelope, aligning the surface. The retrograde interior acts as an angular-momentum reservoir, while interior--envelope coupling slows the surface rotation. A semi-empirical relation gives an envelope--interior angular-momentum exchange timescale of $\sim4$~Myr, similar to the observed orbital-decay timescale of $\sim3.25$~Myr. The angular-momentum budget also permits this initially retrograde evolution. In contrast, an initially prograde planet would have spun up the surface rotation to a rate substantially higher than observed.

background.title: Bianchi cosmologies with four-dimensional groups of motion in New General Relativity
background.abstract: We study the dynamics of the most general metric teleparallel spacetimes of Bianchi types II, III and IX, which admit a four-dimensional symmetry group, in the 1-parameter family of New General Relativity. We first show that in each of these classes the most general metric teleparallel geometry is described by four free functions of time, while another four functions of time describe the most general energy-momentum tensor compatible with the same symmetries. We then derive the field equations of New General Relativity for this class of geometries. Finally, we present some solutions to these field equations. Our results show that both solutions resembling features of the standard Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker cosmology of General Relativity and deviations thereof exist.

background.title: Root-of-Unity Limits of Trigonometric qKZ Connections
background.abstract: Over the field of complex numbers, we study root-of-unity limits of trigonometric qKZ connections associated with tensor products of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ Verma modules and of their hypergeometric solutions. As the multiplicative step approaches a primitive $m$-th root of unity and the quantum-group and twist parameters approach $1$, the $m$-step qKZ transport yields, on every fixed-degree subspace,a differential connection. We show that this connection is the pullback of the trigonometric KZ connection under the power map $z\mapsto z^m$, with the KZ parameter rescaled by $m$, and establish formal and $\ell$-adic versions. In degree one, with all highest weights equal to $1$, we determine the limits of normalized qKZ hypergeometric circle integrals in arbitrary angular chambers. The limits are expressed in terms of loaded hypergeometric integrals for the trigonometric KZ equations and explicit chamber-dependent upper-triangular matrices. We establish compatibility of the resulting distinguished fundamental matrices under inward analytic continuation, governed by the right weak Bruhat order,and under power maps, including composition of root orders.

background.title: Exact Spherical Branes and Deformations: BMN, IKKT and $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$
background.abstract: We present a unified analytic solution to the BPS equations of spherical Dp-branes for $1\leq p \leq 5$ and give the corresponding type II uplifts in closed form. These are holographically dual to maximally supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^{p+1}$. The change of variables that makes the BPS equations integrable also allows us to analytically calculate a universal result for the holographic Wilson loop and obtain UV asymptotic behaviour previously determined numerically. The same change of variables extends naturally, with suitable modifications, to the cases $p=0$ and $p=-1$. We obtain a 1-parameter family of D0-brane solutions and show how the IR conditions lead to a singular limit of the integration constant. We also solve the D(-1)-brane BPS equations and show the resulting Euclidean uplift fails regularity conditions. Separately, we obtain an explicit representation of the one-ball electrostatic solution of polarised IKKT, which lets us express multipole moments and holographic observables using elliptic invariants. Finally, we analytically solve the BPS equations of the holographic dual of $\mathcal{N}=2^\ast$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory on $S^4$, present the corresponding type IIB uplift and calculate the holographic Wilson loop.

background.title: Neutral hydrogen in the Shapley Supercluster core II. Gas content and star formation in the filaments connecting the core
background.abstract: We investigate the neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) content of galaxies across the Shapley Supercluster (SSC) at z = 0.048 by combining new deep MeerKAT L band observations of five filament pointings with archival MeerKAT Galaxy Cluster Legacy Survey observations of the supercluster core. Together with optical data from the Shapley Supercluster Survey, these observations provide a homogeneous view of galaxy evolution from the virialised cluster environment to the surrounding filaments. We compare the HI content, star formation activity, gas depletion timescales, and morphological properties of galaxies relative to the gas fraction and star forming main sequences. The global HI detection fraction increases from 30 per cent in the cluster centre to 45 per cent in the filaments. While HI detected galaxies in the cluster centre are dominated by transition zone systems, the filament population is shared nearly equally between star forming main sequence and transition zone detections, indicating ongoing environmental transformation. Their gas properties also differ: cluster galaxies exhibit progressively depleted HI reservoirs towards the red sequence, whereas filament galaxies remain primarily gas rich. Within the filaments, long HI depletion timescales exceeding the Hubble time are concentrated in specific populations, notably 71 per cent of transition zone and 57 per cent of gas rich detections, indicating the inefficient conversion of atomic gas into stars. The HI detected filament population is dominated by late type galaxies, while the underlying non detected population is primarily composed of early type systems, consistent with environmental pre processing before cluster infall.

background.title: Connecting Coronal Loop Scaling Laws and Kink Wave Heating: An Analytical and Numerical Study
background.abstract: Turbulent dissipation of kink waves has been proposed as one of the mechanisms responsible for the observed high coronal temperatures. We test this hypothesis by examining the effect of this heating mechanism on coronal loops. The coronal loop static and dynamic behaviour is investigated under the assumption that the heating in the loop is primarily provided by kink wave dissipation. The heating term is borrowed from the recently developed UAWSoM model. Loop modelling is done in 1D using three different methods: one analytical following the principles first set in the RTV scaling laws, and two numerical: one based on the setup used to derive the RTVS scaling laws, and UAWSoM. We provide scaling laws and estimate density, temperature, and pressure, as well as kink wave heating rate and kink wave energy density needed to counteract energy loss by thermal conduction and radiative cooling. Estimates of kink wave energy density needed to heat the loop to 1 MK correspond to maximum velocity amplitudes of around 35 km s$^{-1}$ near the loop apex. Loop radius, density contrast and filling factor are found to affect the predictions significantly. The two numerical methods agree to a high degree. The analytical method predicts that $W_\textrm{k} \propto PL^{-2/3}$, while the two numerical methods show a wider range of scaling exponents which depend on the location in the loop. UAWSoM simulations suggest that loops may exhibit dynamic behaviour for a wide range of loop conditions, which may include thermal non-equilibrium cycles and periods of emerging and dissipating slow waves. Overall, estimates of kink wave energy density and scaling laws provide observational constraints on the importance of the proposed kink wave heating mechanism, with the current preliminary results suggesting that the uniturbulent kink wave heating may be a significant source of energy and heat in coronal loops.

background.title: Flux-induced condensation in a radial geometry
background.abstract: Stirring and shear usually suppress phase separation, but transport through a boundary can induce it. We study a binary mixture that is stable everywhere at rest and fills a two-dimensional annulus. The inner boundary is semipermeable and exchanges material with a permeate held at a fixed chemical potential, so that a steady flux of one component crosses the annulus. Although this driven system carries a steady current and produces entropy, within Model B dynamics its steady state is an equilibrium profile in an effective external field that is logarithmic in the distance from the center. Its strength is not imposed from outside but set by the permeate and the permeability of the boundary. Above a threshold driving flux, a condensed annulus forms around the inner boundary. It is bounded by a stationary front whose radius depends exponentially on the ratio of the bulk driving force to the flux. The front is pinned by the effective field and does not coarsen, and the threshold flux decreases only as the inverse logarithm of the system size. The driving flux shifts the phase lines but leaves the critical temperature unchanged. Interfacial tension gives rise to a critical nucleus and to a fold, at which the condensed state ceases to exist, with a threshold that we obtain in closed form. Numerical solutions confirm these predictions and reveal a hysteresis loop bounded by two saddle-node bifurcations. By symmetry, the theory also describes cavitation around a sink.

background.title: Geometric Formulation of Covariant Spin Operator
background.abstract: In relativistic quantum theory, Lorentz boosts induce momentum-dependent Wigner rotations, complicating the coupling of particle spins in arbitrary frames. We describe particle spin spaces as fibers of an associate bundle over the velocity manifold, and different particle's spins residing at distinct fibers. Analogy to general relativity, we introduce parallel transport to bring spins at different velocities into a common frame, where they can be coupled. Using spinor-helicity variables, we construct the parallel transport operator along geodesics and show how it is uniquely determined by little group covariance. This construction gives explicit form of the covariant spin and orbital operators, and yields a covariant 3-point amplitude basis with definite spin and orbital angular momentum. Higher-point amplitudes can be constructively obtained and applied to the covariant partial wave expansion for amplitudes, form factors, and correlation functions, etc.

background.title: A Faà di Bruno Convolution Identity in Parafermion Operator Products
background.abstract: We give a detailed combinatorial proof of a Faà di Bruno convolution identity used in parafermion operator-product calculations. The identity establishes the cancellation of potentially more singular terms and shows that the leading contribution combines the polynomial indices additively. The proof, originating in the author's doctoral thesis, provides a general derivation of an identity stated in earlier parafermion literature.

background.title: Full-Color Two-loop Four-point Form Factor in N=4 SYM with Global CK-duality
background.abstract: We determine the full-color two-loop four-point MHV form factor of the stress-tensor supermultiplet in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. Using color-kinematics (CK) duality and unitarity cuts, we construct complete one- and two-loop integrands manifesting global off-shell CK duality without explicit $μ^2$ dependence. Integration-by-parts reduction to uniform-transcendentality master integrals yields purely rational numbers multiplying simple kinematic prefactors, manifesting maximal transcendentality. Expressing the form factor in terms of pentagon functions, we verify full-color infrared-pole cancellation, extract the finite remainder, and obtain new non-planar results for the two-loop triple-collinear splitting function and double-soft current.

background.title: Global existence versus blow-up for Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattices
background.abstract: This paper investigates the global behavior of infinite nonlinear lattices. In particular, for the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam--Tsingou-$α$ lattice (FPUT-$α$), we show global existence for small initial data via a region-based approach, and prove blow-up for negative energy and some positive energy, given appropriate conditions on the initial momentum and dispersion. Moreover, we extend these results to the nonlinear Klein-Gordon (DNKG) equation and nonlinear wave (DNW) equation. \

background.title: Pure integral formula of spinfoam amplitude and curvature corrections in effective theory
background.abstract: We develop a new analytic method for the semiclassical analysis of the Lorentzian EPRL spinfoam amplitude on a fixed triangulation. We derive a pure integral formula for the spinfoam amplitude that trades the discrete sum over internal spins for integrals over continuous variables. This reformulation is free of discrete sums and provides a well-behaved action that is well-adapted to the stationary phase approximation in the large-spin regime. Integrating out the non-geometric variables yields an effective action for the edge lengths of the Regge geometry. Applying the stationary phase approximation and expanding this effective action to second order in perturbations around a flat background, we obtain the classical Regge action at leading order, supplemented by a quadratic correction in the deficit angles $\varepsilon$. This curvature correction originates from two distinct sources: a holonomy correction resulting from the new action and the fluctuations of non-Regge areas. We show that the quadratic $\varepsilon$ correction appears at a higher order in the Barbero-Immirzi parameter $γ$ relative to the Regge action. Together with the large-spin expansion, this yields a two-parameter expansion for the spinfoam effective action, whose leading order is the quadratic Regge action. In the long wavelength regime, the latter approaches the action of a massless spin-2 graviton.

background.title: Tunable Ground-State Entanglement in Fully Connected Quantum Systems: From Logarithmic to Volume-Law Scaling
background.abstract: Entanglement scaling is a central probe of the complexity of quantum many-body ground states, yet once geometric locality is absent, it can depend sensitively on the structure and normalization of interactions. For fully connected Hamiltonians with the natural Kac normalization, nondegenerate gapped ground states are known to obey a logarithmic entanglement bound. Here we ask how the ground-state entanglement changes when this interaction normalization is continuously relaxed away from the Kac scale. We answer this question by constructing an explicit all-to-all bipartite Hamiltonian of $n$ qubits with Fourier pairing amplitudes and pairwise interaction strength proportional to $n^{-κ}$. For sufficiently small fixed coupling, we prove that every pure ground state has entanglement entropy $Θ(n^{2-2κ} \log n)$ for $1/2<κ\leq1$ and $Θ(n)$ at $κ=1/2$. We further show that the ground state is unique and separated from the rest of the spectrum by a system-size-independent gap for $3/4 \leq κ\leq 1$, while weak-coupling analysis and numerical calculations suggest that the gap remains open also for $1/2 \leq κ< 3/4$. Thus, varying only the interaction normalization yields a controlled hierarchy from logarithmic scaling at the natural Kac normalization $κ=1$ to increasingly strong subextensive entanglement and ultimately to a volume law, showing that even an arbitrarily weak relaxation of this normalization precludes a universal logarithmic entanglement bound.

background.title: Geometric control of diffusive relaxation: spectral design, transport bounds and transverse mode isolation
background.abstract: Geometric confinement changes both thermal relaxation and heat throughput, but these effects need not be governed by the same conduction path. We establish a distinction between serial and parallel geometries for passive, homogeneous Fourier conductors at fixed material properties, volume and length. For a reduced variable-area conductor, two logarithmic shape harmonics independently tune two selected Bloch-rate pairs, and exact local transport level sets permit spectral redistribution at fixed effective diffusivity. A nonperturbative weighted Poincaré bound, however, requires the effective axial diffusivity to vanish if the first positive insulated rate tends to zero at fixed length. This obstruction is avoided by continuous parallel paths with weak transverse exchange. Capacity-weighted networks identify the exchange mechanism, and a three-dimensional product domain provides an exact bulk realization. Its axial conductance remains $κV/L^2$, while exactly one positive insulated rate vanishes and the next approaches a positive limit set by axial, chamber and neck diffusion. The slow rate is asymptotically the transverse neck conductance times the sum of inverse chamber capacities. Spectral projection estimates translate this separation into a preparation- and readout-dependent observation window. The result is metastable retention of a temperature contrast under insulated conditions, not a second equilibrium state. It identifies when geometrical control of internal equilibration can be separated from macroscopic heat transport.

background.title: Asymmetric Orbifolds and 4-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ String Islands
background.abstract: We formulate heterotic and type II $\mathbb T^6/\mathbb Z_n$ asymmetric orbifolds preserving all 16 right-moving supersymmetries and leading to 4-dimensional islands without massless moduli other than the dilaton. We establish the consistency of the orbifold conformal field theory, including the validity of operator interpretation. In the heterotic case we classify all islands based on the $Γ(22,6)$ lattice constructed via the Leech lattice. In the type II case we also provide a classification of allowed $Γ(6,6)$ lattices and orbifold generators. In both cases we further examine whether a particular orbifold admits an archipelago of different islands arising from inequivalent realizations of the orbifold action.

background.title: Interpretation follows computation for deformed atomic nuclei
background.abstract: The interpretation of nuclear levels in experiments and ab initio computations is challenging because it requires the production and analysis of many expectation values and transition strengths. Here we introduce an approach that yields directly interpretable states. Our ab initio coupled-cluster computations start from a reference state with axial symmetry and positive parity. Equation-of-motion techniques then yield intrinsic states with definite parity and angular-momentum projection onto the symmetry axis. Finally, the projection onto good angular momenta yields rotational bands based on these intrinsic states. In the neutron-rich nucleus $^{34}$Mg, where only the ground-state band is known, we find several low-lying positive- and negative-parity bands. The lowest, a $K^π=3^-$ band, is dominated by a single neutron particle-hole excitation rather than by octupole collectivity. These results challenge the common wisdom about how deformation and pairing work in nuclei.

background.title: A Computational and Experimental Framework for Fourier Optics in Python
background.abstract: Simulation of the propagation of light is useful for the design and dimensioning of optical systems. In this paper, we present the basics of propagation simulation using Fourier optics and practical implementation in Python, with a particular emphasis on dimensions. We first verify that our numerical wave-optics simulations maintain correct physical spatial scaling. Next, we benchmark numerical propagation against closed-form analytical formulas for Gaussian beams, lens focusing effects, and grating diffraction. We then show how those simulations can be used to generate diffractive optical elements such as Fresnel zone plates, and we bridge the gap between numerical simulations and experiments by collecting data and recovering phase information using a phase retrieval algorithm.

background.title: Elliptic analogues of KP and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions
background.abstract: We develop a tau-function framework for soliton solutions on elliptic backgrounds associated with the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili (KP) hierarchy and its B-type counterpart (BKP). Starting from discrete KP (dKP) and discrete BKP (dBKP) equations of elliptic type, we construct Casorati and Gram determinant tau functions for the elliptic dKP through Darboux and binary Darboux transformations, and elliptic Pfaffian tau functions for dBKP through the Moutard transformation. Moreover, the higher-order discrete KP and BKP hierarchies together with their tau functions are constructed via Pfaffian identities. Then, through Miwa transformations, the continuous elliptic KP, modified KP, and BKP hierarchies and their tau functions are provided. Suitable constraints on spectral parameters or wave numbers yield reductions to the Korteweg--de Vries (KdV), focusing and defocusing modified Korteweg--de Vries (mKdV), and Sawada--Kotera (SK) equations, together with their solutions on elliptic backgrounds. We also construct KP line-soliton solutions and obtain lump solutions for the KP-I equation. For selected determinant families, we establish sufficient conditions for real-valuedness and global nonsingularity. The resulting framework provides a common approach to elliptic tau functions, their discrete and continuous bilinear identities, and the construction of solutions through reductions.
